title: Guide
text: NARUTO WORLD: EMBER CORPS JUTSU COMPENDIUM VOLUME IV Jutsu rules, techniques, Eight Gates, Shadow Clones, summoning, natural chakra and hyper elements. “A jutsu is only a tool until somebody makes it unmistakably theirs.” | Volume | Book | Primary Use | | I | Core Rules | Character creation, attributes, skills, advancement, abilities, combat, wounds and downtime. | | II | Uniques | Character-defining traits, upgrade chains and expanded playstyle options. | | III | Clans & Lineages | The Five Gre

title: Explanation
text: The core of a ninja's supernatural capabilities comes from their jutsu--meaning, literally, techniques. These use chakra, either projected outwards or used to amplify one's physical performance, to perform feats that would be literally impossible for a normal person. These are divided into three broad categories: taijutsu, ninjutsu, and genjutsu. Taijutsu, or body techniques, use the chakra flowing throughout a ninja's body to give them the exceptional speed or strength needed to perform the tec

title: Rule
text: Each jutsu is a unique action that, once you've learned it, you can perform. All jutsu are divided into five main ranks (E, D, C, B, and A), with S-rank techniques being rare techniques known only to their inventor and perhaps a handful of people that person taught them to. Though each rank of each type has special requirements to learn (explained in more detail in the relevant sections), a few broad rules apply. For example, to learn ninjutsu of one of the five elements, you need the appropriat

title: Reader's Guide
text: Most of the jutsu entries have a lot of information packed into them. To help make them easier to read, a lot of the common factors are written using shorthand; for example, rather than spelling out "Using this technique requires you to make a Chakra Exhaustion roll against 10", a jutsu would have an entry of "Chakra: 10" Below are all the common terms you'll see in jutsu entries, and what they mean.

title: Stamina / Chakra
text: The technique's Stamina and Chakra cost, respectively.

title: Upkeep
text: Some techniques require a constant expenditure of your energy to maintain; this is what upkeep represents. So long as you maintain these techniques (which typically can be done indefinitely) you suffer a penalty to all Stamina and Chakra Exhaustion rolls equal to that technique's Upkeep. If you're maintaining multiple techniques with Upkeeps, these penalties stack. If your total Upkeep/2 exceeds your bonus to Chakra Exhaustion rolls (including penalties), you automatically advance a Fatigue leve

title: Damage
text: The base damage dealt by the technique. You add your damage bonus (multiplied by the attack's modified Speed) to this number.

title: Accuracy
text: Some jutsu have bonuses or penalties to accuracy. If there's no entry for this, it uses your normal accuracy.

title: Range
text: How many yards away the attack's target can be. In the case of area-of-effect techniques, they can be centered anywhere within this range (and their effects may well extend beyond it). If it has no range then it is centered on yourself (in which case it does not affect you).

title: Area
text: The area of a jutsu which can come in any of 3 forms below: Area X: A radius plain and simple using the radius for dodge penalties Line X, Y: A rectangle with a width of X and a length of Y using the lower of the 2 values for dodge penalties. Cube X: A square X by X yards using X for dodge penalties When dodging an AoE Jutsu you must first find out if you are fast enough to escape it. Take the speed of the attack and compare how far you could move in that IC to the Area of the jutsu. If your spe

title: Speed
text: The jutsu's base Speed.

title: Seal Speed
text: The jutsu's base seal speed.

title: Special
text: Any Special status effect requires a Chakra Control roll against the target's Resistance unless its Jutsu or the status rules say otherwise. Stun, Knockback and conditions inflicted by Clan Jutsu do not require an additional status roll unless their entry explicitly requires one. Genjutsu resolve their listed effects using Genjutsu Offense against Genjutsu Defense instead.

title: Tags
text: At a glance of what the jutsu can achieve. Additional tags can be found for taijutsu and ninjutsu in their respective areas. Here are the following general tags and their meanings: Type of Action Attack | It's an attack they need to directly defend against. Interrupt | It can be used in response to an action, usually an attack. Utility | It does something useful…probably Link | Added on to another action increasing its speed, fatigue cost, and whatever else. This does not change any tag, rank, o

title: Effects
text: Any special characteristics of a technique which aren't covered by one of the above categories are listed here.

title: Requirements
text: Taijutsu is more than just hand-to-hand combat; ninjutsu techniques go well beyond the realm of what's possible for normal humans, smashing rocks and the like. It's not exactly... easy. There are three ways to qualify to learn a taijutsu technique: the first is your rank in the Athletics skill. If you're in good enough physical condition, you can pull off some pretty impressive things. The second, Research skill rank, sufficient understanding of how the move should be executed allows you to make

title: Limb Requirements
text: Many taijutsu require you to have x arms and/or legs free to utilize them. These come in the form of Tags: X Arms or X Legs with X being the amount of limbs free and usable for the technique.

title: Requirements
text: Learning ninjutsu is a great deal of work; a ninja has to learn how to mold their chakra, how to convert it to the right elemental nature, then how to properly project it, along with memorizing all the necessary handseals... for each individual jutsu they know. There are three ways you can qualify to learn ninjutsu of a given rank. The first is Chakra Control skill ranks: With sufficient control over your chakra it becomes easier to mold it efficiently, and mold the vast amounts of chakra used i

title: Elemental Strength and Weaknesses
text: All Elemental jutsu follow a strengths and weakness chart that circles back on itself. The strengths and weaknesses go as follows: Earth \> Water \> Fire \> Wind \> Lightning \> Earth

title: Created weapons, enhanced attacks and you!
text: Weapons and ninjutsu that empower taijutsu have a few special effects. First, when created they count as ninjutsu (for cases of chakra rolls and the like), however, when attacking they count as taijutsu. This means they do not gain the bonuses from things such as specialist which empower ninjutsu, they would only gain it from taijutsu. They do count as their element when opposing different elements, however. This applies to dual-elements effects as well. Created weapons only count for their elem

title: Bunshin
text: Bunshin, unless stated otherwise, act 1 IC after they were created and have a cap of 3 at a time. If they were created before the initiative, then they act on their user's IC. Clones can ONLY perform actions listed in their action options. Bunshin act on their own IC, separate from their creator, and using them does not increase the user's speed unless explicitly mentioned. As they are separate entities, they do NOT benefit from any jutsu you use that designates you, such as Kage Buyou. They wou

text: E-Rank Bukijutsu is universally available to player characters. | Rank | Athletics | Research | | E | — | — | | D | 4 | 5 | | C | 10 | 12 | | B | 20 | 22 | | A | 30 | 32 | B-Rank and A-Rank: the normal mentor rule still applies. You must be taught the technique unless you exceed the relevant learning requirement by 50%, following the general Jutsu rules.

title: Buki Attacks
text: Unless a technique lists fixed Damage or Speed, an attacking Bukijutsu starts from the Basic Weapon Attack of the weapon being used and applies the modifiers printed in the technique. “dS” uses that weapon’s base damage die size. A weapon attack may only be modified or replaced by one Bukijutsu unless another technique explicitly has the Link tag. Chain tags are not Link tags. If your weapon has an innate delay, any Bukijutsu you cast gains a Delay equal to half your weapon’s delay. If a Bukijut

title: Chain
text: Chain Value: A Chain is tracked against one target and has a value of 0, 1 or 2. It has no passive damage bonus. Chain 1 — Entry: May be used at Chain 0. On a hit, establish Chain 1 against that target. A successful Chain 1 during an existing Chain resets the value to 1. Chain 2 — Pressure: Requires Chain 1 or 2 against that target. On a hit, set the Chain to 2. Further Chain 2 techniques may be used while at 2 and keep the value at 2. Chain 3 — Finisher: Requires Chain 2 against that target. Th

title: Fan Bridge
text: Fan Bukijutsu has a deliberate exception to the normal Chain break rule. Wind Bridge may carry one Fan-tagged Fuuton through an active Chain. The Fuuton remains Ninjutsu, never becomes Chain 1/2/3, receives no Bukijutsu damage or status riders, and does not refresh the Chain Window. But your chain doesn’t break. You can do this once per chain.

title: Genjutsu Requirements
text: Genjutsu isn't easy. In fact, genjutsu is really, really hard, even by the standards of other ninja techniques. Taijutsu and ninjutsu are both, after enough shinobi training, slightly intuitive; and, in the case of the latter, every ninja has an elemental affinity they can rely on to help them out even when they struggle overall. Not so with genjutsu. There is no such thing as an 'affinity' for it (though some ninja who seem to have an easier time learning it are occasionally described as such),

title: Fūinjutsu Requirements
text: Fūinjutsu, or sealing techniques, are, as the name suggests, techniques which use chakra to form specialized 'seals'. They're difficult to use, and have limited combat viability. What makes them useful is that these seals are stable. Normally, any sort of chakra-based effect will expire soon after its user stops applying chakra to it, the energy dissipating back into the world. Seals don't, and depending on the individual seal and the skill of the user some can last for decades if left undisturb

title: Medical Ninjutsu
text: One of the few good things the development of ways to control chakra has brought to the world is the appropriately named medical ninjutsu. These are techniques which safely transfer chakra to another person, or use it to accelerate the natural healing process, cure maladies, and otherwise ameliorate suffering and avoid unnecessary casualties. Medical ninjutsu also has a darker side. The pioneers in the field learned the secrets of the human body so that they could help people, but more than a ha

title: Unarmed Taijutsu
text: Not much to say here. You hit people with your fists, feet, and in all manner of other creative ways. These techniques can stand on their own but contains integral pieces for Combo and Grapple jutsu.

title: Deashi Harai: Foot Sweep
text: You cause an opponent to fall down by knocking their legs out from under them. Calling it a 'technique' is misleadinKenjutsug, but there's more to unbalancing a ninja than just wanting to; it does take at least a little bit of training. Stamina: 8 Speed: 4 Accuracy: +2 Special: Prone Tags: Attack, Melee Effects: If used while in a grapple its Special: is replaced by the following: Takedown, Control 8.

title: Feint
text: A subtle trick that almost every ninja knows--and knows how to detect. Still, those that are particularly adept at it are often difficult to defend against properly. Stamina: +2 Speed: +2 Tags: Link Effects: This is added to any other melee-range Unarmed or Combo Attack, and increases that action's Stamina and Speed by 2 each. title: Headbutt
text: You use your head to hit someone else's head. Really, honestly, it's a highly technical process. You just don't understand because you're not a ninja. Stamina: 10 Damage: STR Speed: 7 Accuracy: -1 Tags: Attack, Melee Effects: This always deals a head wound and you must take the final wounding damage, if that would cause you a wound then you gain a head wound of that severity. When used while in a grapple this jutsu gains: Pummel, Control 1

title: Dainamikku Entorii - Dynamic Entry
text: This technique is nothing more than a jumpkick at an opponent from hiding. The hiding part became required because of genin's tendency to shout out things like "HIYAH!" as they did it. Stamina: 16 Damage: (STR/4)d6 Speed: 12 Special: Requires you be hidden from your target. Tags: Attack, Blunt, Melee Effects: After the first time Dynamic Entry has been used in combat (by you, by someone else, it doesn't matter) it has a -6 Accuracy for the rest of that battle.

title: Flash Step
text: You make small decisive leaps allowing you to effectively close the distance between you and your enemy. Stamina: + X / 3 (rounded up) Speed: X / 3 (rounded up) Tags: Link Effects: This is used alongside a melee Taijutsu or Kenjutsu attack, increasing your move with attack by X yards to a maximum of the speed of the jutsu.

title: Irimiseme - Entering Attack
text: Rather then a direct attack this jutsu involves stepping into close range with an opponent and deflecting a weapon or jutsu by targeting their wrist or elbow. Stamina: 8 + X\3 Speed: 4 Tags: Interrupt Effects: X is the rank of the jutsu being parried. This may be used to parry any weapon attack or attack ninjutsu performed in melee range. The speed of this interrupt cannot be reduced below 2.

title: Konoha Senpū - Leaf Whirlwind
text: A low sweep forces the guard down before a high turning kick carries the real impact. Stamina: 12 Damage: 8d8 Accuracy: +1 Range: Melee Speed: 10 Special: Stun 3 Tags: Attack, Melee, Blunt, Opener Effects: On a full hit, you may choose to apply Knockback 2 or begin a Combo with this target. If used as a Combo Opener, its Momentum grants +1 Accuracy to the next Combo Jutsu only.

title: Reppuu - Gale
text: With alarming quickness you drop low to the ground and perform a full 360-degree sweeping kick that knocks opponents off their feet when they attempt to close in for an attack of their own. Stamina: 13 Damage: (STR/7)d10 Speed: 8 Tags: Attack, Interrupt, Opener, Blunt, Melee Effects: Gale may (but doesn’t require to) be used as an interrupt after you have successfully dodged an attack, targeting the attacker. If Gale is used after a dodge in this fashion, the dodge roll replaces Gale's accuracy.

title: Senpuu - Whirlwind
text: The user rotates while extending one leg, starting with a high roundhouse that's used partially as a feint. Whether it hits or misses, they continue to rotate into a second spin aimed at the lower part of the body. Stamina: 16 Damage: (STR/6)d8 Speed: 12 Area: 2 Special: Opener Tags: Attack, Blunt, Melee Effects: This attack hits all enemies in range. title: Teiryuu Dageki - Halting Blow
text: In one smooth motion, the user extends their arm and pushes aside an oncoming blow, steps inward and pulls back their forearm to slam their elbow into the opponent, turning their defense into their offense. Stamina: 13 Damage: (STR/6)d4 Speed: 5 Tags: Opener, Interrupt Effects: Halting Blow may be used as an unarmed parry, with a +3 bonus. If you successfully defend, Halting Blow immediately acts as an attack at no extra cost, using the results of your parry roll as its Accuracy. Momentum: Parri

title: Throw
text: You use leverage, brute force, or a combination of the two to physically throw an enemy, either by flipping them over you, hurling them into a nearby object, slamming them to the ground, or something similar. Stamina: 14 Damage: (STR/10)d20 Speed: 8 Accuracy: -2 Special: Stun 4 Tags: Attack, Blunt, Melee Effects: If used while in a grapple it gains the following: Takedown, Control 8

title: Tokken - Thrusting Shoulder
text: By charging forward and turning at the last moment to bring a shoulder out front, the user slams into the enemy, knocking them back. It relies mostly on the weight of the user, with the expectation they'll be heavier than the person they're running into. Stamina: 10 Damage: (RES/5)d8 Speed: 10 Tags: Attack, Blunt, Melee Effects: This knocks the victim back (your RES)/10 yards.

title: Attsu Buchikomu - Pain Driver
text: A brutal technique, and completely inappropriate for training (because someone would have thought it was okay, if we didn't say that). The attacker finds a weak point on their opponent's body, the site of a previous injury, and strikes there to amplify the existing wound. Stamina: 18 Damage: (STR/5)d4 Speed: 12 Tags: Attack, Blunt, Melee Effects: This attack must be a called shot, and does not normally inflict wounds. Instead, if it targets a location with a Minor Blunt wound, that wound is remo

title: Bōshi Riken - Spinning Backfist
text: With a burst of chakra to one of the user's legs, they spin around and extend an arm to knock an opponent senseless with the back of their fist. It's a powerful blow as it uses the weight and momentum of the user's entire body, but has an inherent weakness of losing sight of the enemy while spinning. Stamina: 24 Damage: (STR/7)d12 Accuracy: -3 Speed: 10 Tags: Attack, Blunt, Melee Effects: This technique's damage is tripled when determining the severity of wounds it inflicts.

title: Chouyaku Kage Kaihi no Jutsu - Leaping Shadow Evasion Technique
text: You leap away from an attack, getting yourself safely out of range. However, you don't pause to regain your orientation and settle into your new position, instead keeping ready to move again. Stamina: 18 Speed: 4 Tags: Utility, Interrupt Effects: When you use Chouyaku Kage Kaihi, make a dodge roll. You may automatically attempt to dodge any incoming attacks, without having to take an action to do so, using Chouyaku Kage Kaihi's result as your effective dodge roll. This lasts until you take any a

title: Daisenpuu - Great Whirlwind
text: A more complex version of Senpuu which involves three kicks to the target's body going in the reverse order as before, starting low and going high to end with an axe kick to the opponent's head. The speed and constant rotation is strong enough to actually lift the practitioner into the air during execution. Stamina: 22 Damage: (STR/6)d12 Speed: 14 Area: 3 Requires: Senpuu Special: Opener Tags: Opener, Blunt, Melee Effects: This attack hits all enemies in range. If partial defense applies, you de

title: Konoha Dai Senpū - Leaf Great Whirlwind
text: A chain of turning kicks expands the basic whirlwind into a pressure sequence. Stamina: 20 Damage: 16d8 Range: Melee Speed: 14 Special: Stun 5 Tags: Attack, Melee, Blunt Effects: If the target is Prone or suffering Immobilization 3+, gain +2 Accuracy but do not increase damage. On a full hit you may move 2 yards around the target without provoking any movement-triggered effects from that target.

title: Maboroshi Tejun - Phantom Step
text: Despite the fancy name, it's a fairly simple 'technique'. With a momentary burst of energy (and probably adrenaline, considering the circumstances where it's likely to be used) the user does their best to get out of the way of an impending attack. The "phantom" came mostly from the way a shinobi using this can, to the untrained eye, seems to almost disappear. And because ninjas thought it sounded cool. Stamina: 5 \ X Speed: +X Tags: Link Effects: X has a maximum of 5. This is used alongside a do

title: No Design, No Conception
text: When words and actions are spontaneously the same. You move forwards at the exact same time as your opponent and in doing so throw off their rhythm. Of course, the spontaneous nature of this technique makes it impossible to have any rhythm of your own to attack with, but the practiced shinobi can take advantage of the situation to grab ahold of their opponent. Stamina: 5 + 5\X Speed: + X Tags: Link Effects: X has a maximum of 5. This technique is used alongside any interrupt that requires a defe

title: Ryuorosu - Dragon Takedown
text: Adapted--in purpose, method, and name--from a 'normal' style of martial arts, the Dragon Takedown is a more aggressive method of initiating a grapple, often throwing an opponent to the ground in the process. Stamina: 26 Damage: (STR/8)d12 Speed: 18 Tags: Attack, Blunt, Melee Effects: If you hit, you initiate a clinch with your opponent but you gain a -10 to your control. Then you may immediately attempt a Submission for no cost.

title: Souji Reppuu - Sweeping Gale
text: By flipping forward into a crouch, the user builds momentum that's used to instantly land and begin spinning on one foot, extending the other leg out while using chakra to enhance its density, rotating repeatedly to strike the knees of the enemy, simultaneously evading and tripping them. Stamina: 19 Damage: (STR/6)d8 Speed: 8 Special: Prone Requires: Deashi Harai: Foot Sweep, Reppuu Tags: Attack, Interrupt, Opener, Blunt, Melee Effects: This follows the rules for the D-rank Reppuu technique (inc

title: Suplex
text: The user secures the opponent around the torso or hips, shifts their center of gravity, and drives them over the shoulder or backward into the ground. The technique is less about raw lifting strength than committing to the throw before the opponent can recover their footing. Stamina: 18 Damage: (STR/5)d10 Speed: 15 Accuracy: -3 Tags: Attack, Blunt, Melee Effects: When used while in a Grapple this jutsu gains: Pummel, Control 6. If Suplex inflicts a wound, it is dealt to the opponent's head.

title: Tsutenkyaku - Painful Sky Leg
text: After concentrating chakra in the user's legs, they leap high into the air and come down in a destructive axe kick, using gravity to enhance the momentum behind the blow while the user's chakra is used to enhance the destructive force of the blow. Stamina: 25 Damage: (STR/20)d20 Area: 6 Speed: 16 Special: -6 Accuracy Tags: Attack, Blunt, Melee Effects: Your damage bonus is doubled for this attack. title: Uchikudakute no Jutsu - Shattering Hand Technique
text: Ninja can perform incredible feats of strength; after years of grueling training, some can literally reduce boulders to gravel for their bare fists. That's a handy trick to have, but most ninja aren't willing to go through the whole 'years of pain and hard work' part, so instead they invented a jutsu which accomplishes a similar effect: by channelling vibrating chakra through their hand at the moment of impact, most solid objects can be shattered with a single blow. title: Bukijutsu
text: Bukijutsu builds on normal weapon attacks rather than replacing them. A Basic Weapon Attack remains the efficient, reliable option; Bukijutsu gives a weapon specialist stronger ways to exploit positioning, repeated defenses, reach, terrain, movement, and other openings. The core Chain structure is unchanged, but it is slightly more forgiving so using a sensible weapon action does not immediately erase the sequence you have built.

title: Learning Requirements
text: E-Rank Bukijutsu is universally available to player characters. E-Rank — Athletics -; Research -. D-Rank — Athletics 4; Research 5. C-Rank — Athletics 10; Research 12. B-Rank — Athletics 20; Research 22. A-Rank — Athletics 30; Research 32. B-Rank and A-Rank use the normal mentor rule. You must be taught the technique unless you exceed the relevant learning requirement by 50%, following the general Jutsu rules.

title: Buki Attacks
text: Unless a technique lists fixed Damage or Speed, an attacking Bukijutsu starts from the Basic Weapon Attack of the weapon being used and applies the modifiers printed in the technique. “dS” uses that weapon’s base damage die size. A weapon attack may only be modified or replaced by one Bukijutsu unless another technique explicitly has the Link tag. Chain tags are not Link tags. If your weapon has an innate delay, any Bukijutsu you cast gains a Delay equal to half your weapon’s delay. If a Bukijut

title: Specials and Status Rolls
text: Bukijutsu use the normal Special and Status Roll rules. If a Bukijutsu lists a status in its Special line, use Athletics for the Status Roll unless the technique says otherwise; the target rolls Resistance normally. Stun follows its normal rules and is not separately resisted. A Special attached to a damaging Attack only applies if the Attack still produces an effect after defenses and damage reduction, following the normal rules for statuses. Partial Success reduces a numeric Special in the sam

title: Chain
text: Chain Value: A Chain is tracked against one target and has a value of 0, 1 or 2. It has no passive damage bonus. Chain 1 — Entry: May be used at Chain 0 or 1. On a hit, establish Chain 1 against that target. A successful Chain 1 during an existing Chain keeps the value at 1. Chain 2 — Pressure: Requires Chain 1 or 2 against that target. On a hit, set the Chain to 2. Further Chain 2 techniques may be used while at 2 and keep the value at 2. Chain 3 — Finisher: Requires Chain 2 against that target

title: Fan Bridge
text: Fan Bukijutsu has a deliberate exception to the normal Chain break rule. Seamless Wind may carry one Fan-tagged Fuuton through an active Chain. The Fuuton remains Ninjutsu, never becomes Chain 1/2/3, receives no Bukijutsu damage or status riders, and does not refresh the Chain Window. But your Chain does not break. You can do this once per Chain.

title: Bukijutsu Stances
text: Stances are ordinary Self Upkeep Bukijutsu. You may maintain only one Bukijutsu Stance at a time; activating another ends the first. They do not end merely because you attack, move or defend. They use the normal Upkeep rules, may be activated through Preparation when legal, and interact with generic Upkeep effects only when those effects actually apply to Bukijutsu or to Upkeep generally. Effects written specifically for Ninjutsu Upkeep do not apply. Bukijutsu Stances do not cost XP to learn and

title: High Guard
text: You hold the weapon high enough to threaten the first line immediately, accepting a more exposed defensive posture. Rank: D Stamina: 8 Upkeep: 3 Speed: 6 Tags: Utility, Self, Upkeep, Bukijutsu Stance Effects: Your Chain 1 and Chain 2 Melee Bukijutsu gain +1 Accuracy. Your Dodge and Parry rolls take -1.

title: Low Guard
text: The weapon stays low and close to the body, making it easier to receive an attack before committing to your own. Rank: D Stamina: 8 Upkeep: 3 Speed: 6 Tags: Utility, Self, Upkeep, Bukijutsu Stance Effects: Gain +1 Dodge and Parry. Your damaging Melee Bukijutsu take -1 Accuracy.

title: Long Guard
text: You extend the weapon into the space in front of you and make the opponent fight through its reach before they can reach your body. Rank: D Stamina: 9 Upkeep: 3 Speed: 6 Tags: Utility, Self, Upkeep, Bukijutsu Stance Effects: Gain +1 Reach with Melee Weapons and +1 Parry against attacks that began outside your normal Reach. Your normal movement is reduced by 10%.

title: Open Guard
text: You deliberately leave a line available, using the invitation to make the defender commit before your real angle is chosen. Rank: C Stamina: 12 Upkeep: 4 Speed: 8 Tags: Utility, Self, Upkeep, Bukijutsu Stance Effects: Once per Chain, after the target declares a Defense against your Chain attack, give that Defense -1. Your weapon takes +10% durability damage while maintained.

title: Point Guard
text: You keep the point or striking line fixed on one part of the opponent and sacrifice broader coverage for precision. Rank: C Stamina: 12 Upkeep: 4 Speed: 8 Tags: Utility, Self, Upkeep, Bukijutsu Stance Effects: Reduce Called Shot Accuracy penalties with weapon attacks by 2. Weapon attacks that are not Called Shots take -1 Accuracy.

title: Committed Guard
text: You build every movement around the next heavy commitment, gaining force at the cost of reacting cleanly when the opponent moves first. Rank: B Stamina: 18 Upkeep: 6 Speed: 10 Tags: Utility, Self, Upkeep, Bukijutsu Stance Effects: Damaging Melee Bukijutsu gain +10% Wounding and +1 to listed Stun or Knockback. Your defensive Interrupts count as +2 Base Speed for Defense Validity.

title: Weapon Recovery
text: A weapon on the ground is not “out of the fight”; it is a problem of distance, timing, and who reaches it first. You hook it with a foot, catch a returning cord, snatch it from the dirt, or draw a replacement without surrendering the exchange you already built. Rank: E Stamina: 4 Speed: 3 Tags: Chain X, Utility, Bukijutsu Effects: Draw, pick up, or retrieve one weapon within arm’s reach without changing Chain value.

title: Flowing Guard
text: A practiced stance change should not look like somebody stopping to remember a new pose. You let the old guard collapse naturally into the new one, moving hands, feet, and weapon through positions that remain dangerous the entire time. Rank: D Stamina: 6 Speed: 3 Tags: Chain X, Utility, Bukijutsu Effects: Switch from one active Bukijutsu Stance to another Stance you know. Pay the new Stance’s activation cost.

title: Weapon Breaker
text: When an opponent trusts their weapon to catch yours, you punish the contact itself. The strike is allowed to bite into the defending edge, shaft, guard, or frame at the point of worst leverage, turning a successful defense into a durability problem. Rank: B Stamina: +10 Speed: +2 Tags: Link, Bukijutsu Effects: Use retroactively after your weapon Attack is successfully Parried or Blocked by a weapon. After that Defense resolves, the defending weapon gains +2 additional WDP.

title: Chakra Reinforcement
text: Chakra can make a weapon behave differently without changing what it physically is. You reinforce the part that matters for the injury you want—edge, point, striking face, or a projected chakra surface—letting one familiar weapon answer several kinds of protection. Rank: B Chakra: 22 Upkeep: 5 Speed: 10 Tags: Utility, Self, Upkeep, Bukijutsu Effects: Choose Blunt, Slashing, Piercing or Energy. One held weapon may deal that wound type and gains +2 Damage Bonus.

title: Chakra Reach
text: Shaped chakra extends the weapon’s edge, point, or striking line beyond its physical reach, carrying the threat several yards past the material weapon. Rank: A Chakra: 20 Upkeep: 3 Speed: 10 Tags: Utility, Self, Upkeep, Bukijutsu Effects: One Melee Weapon gains +4 Reach and does not trigger ordinary on-contact punishment caused solely by touching the defender.

title: Sword Bukijutsu
text: Sword is the dueling weapon: it reads defensive habits, changes angle and punishes predictable answers.

title: Rising Cut
text: The cut is meant to raise the opponent’s hands and eyes. A clean hit gives you the choice to press that lifted guard or take the outside angle before they can square up again. title: Chain Weapon Bukijutsu
text: Chain weapons are the control weapon: their dedicated Bukijutsu turn the existing Grapple and Control system into a ranged weapon discipline.

title: Weapon Grapples
text: Chain Weapon Bukijutsu use the existing Grapple system rather than a separate restraint system. When a technique says it initiates a Weapon Grapple, the Chain weapon acts as the limbs maintaining the hold. title: Dual Bukijutsu
text: Dual overloads defensive choices: two weapons force the opponent to repeat, split or expose a defensive answer.

For 20 IC, creatures inside the Area have 30% less movement. The first time each creature leaves the Area, it makes Athletics vs your Athletics; on failure, apply Prone and Immobilization 2 until its next action.

title: Requirements
text: Genjutsu isn't easy. In fact, genjutsu is really, really hard, even by the standards of other ninja techniques. Taijutsu and ninjutsu are both, after enough shinobi training, slightly intuitive; and, in the case of the latter, every ninja has an elemental affinity they can rely on to help them out even when they struggle overall. Not so with genjutsu. There is no such thing as an 'affinity' for it (though some ninja who seem to have an easier time learning it are occasionally described as such),

title: Genjutsu Rolls
text: When using Genjutsu the caster has their Genjutsu Offense and anyone interacting with it (explained below) must roll Genjutsu Defense to defend against it. Though defense is not always rolled immediately. \M3\ Genjutsu Off: 1d20 + XP/400 + Abilities/Uniques \M4\ Genjutsu Def: 1d20 + XP/200 + Abilities/Uniques All Genjutsu fall under 3 types. title: Breaking Genjutsu
text: By their nature, it's hard to realize that one is suffering from the effects of a genjutsu technique. It's possible to be afflicted by a genjutsu that you know and use frequently, with obvious 'tells', and still mistake it for reality--such is the nature of delusions. Every combat Genjutsu states when its victim Realizes the illusion. For Realizes entries, X means the margin by which the user's Genjutsu Offense beat that target's Genjutsu Defense, unless the entry defines another variable. Reali

title: Genkoe - Hallucinatory Voices
text: Despite its name, this technique isn't limited to voices, or even auditory hallucinations. It has no effect at all until the victim begins paying a bit too much attention to their surroundings, at which point the technique begins playing tricks on their senses, causing them to see movement at the corner of their vision and gentle sounds just slightly too vague to place. Chakra: 12 Upkeep: 2 Area: 15 Speed: 8 Seal Speed: 12 Duration: 40 IC Tags: Utility, Area Effects: Choose creatures within Area

title: Mousou Enmu no Jutsu - Illusory Mist Technique
text: Masquerading as a higher-ranked Suiton technique, this creates a light bank of fog which has little effect beyond making the atmosphere a bit chillier. An illusion is then laid on all those present (the user may exclude allies if they wish), tricking them into believing the mist is actually thick enough to be a hindrance. title: Senpuku no Jutsu - Concealment Technique
text: This jutsu allows a ninja to conceal small (or sometimes not so-small) items on their person or in their grasp. This is a fantastic technique for smuggling items or transporting them in secrecy, its utility counteracted only by its vulnerabilities. Chakra: 10 Upkeep: 2 Speed: 10 Seal Speed: 8 Duration: 1 Hour Tags: Utility, Self, Indirect Effects: This completely hides an object from casual observation. For the entire duration the object must remain close to you (like held or in a belt holster).

title: Kasumi Juusha no Jutsu - Mist Servant Technique
text: This jutsu creates clones that phase in and out of the ground as if they were made of a blackish, oil-like liquid. When attacked, the clones regenerate themselves. The clones can be controlled to make it seem as if they're attacking. The user can then time their attacks with those of the clones to remain concealed. text: This illusion causes any afflicted by it to see a massive fireball forming above them which slowly descends. Most prudent shinobi will waste time trying to escape its radius, while those who are more reckless will take the 'attack' head-on, bracing themselves against a blow that never actually comes. Chakra: 15 Range: 25 Area: 15 Speed: 10 Seal Speed: 13 Duration: 20 IC Tags: Attack, Area Effects: Choose creatures in Area; each rolls Genjutsu Defense against the caster's Offense on application.

title: Magen: Narakumi no Jutsu - Demonic Illusion: Hell Viewing Technique
text: The user creates an illusion of spinning leaves around the victim, after the leaves disappear, the illusion begins, showing the victim something they'd rather never see, be it a loved one hurt, a monster of their nightmares, or some other such thing. In most cases, it is easy to identify that the image is fake, due to the unlikeliness of it occurring, but some images still leave a foul sensation in one's mind. title: Shinkirou no Jutsu - Mirage Technique
text: This creates an illusion that can fool a person's sight, hearing, or smell--or, with more effort, two of those, or all three. These can be dynamic (such as a flickering fire or a fluttering curtain), but they can't actually interact with anything. This technique is often a last-ditch resort to escape from a superior adversary, or bypass someone when there's no time to deal with them in direct combat. title: Sakki - Killing Intent
text: A side-effect of learning how to control chakra is the ability to sense, and exude, what shinobi refer to as killing intent. More powerful shinobi can project it more strongly, and even send lesser ninja running with just a glance. This genjutsu simulates an intense blast of paralyzingly strong killing intent in an attempt to overwhelm its target. Chakra: 30 Range: 15 Speed: 15 Seal Speed: 20 Duration: 20 + X IC (maximum 60 IC) Special: Stun 5 + X Tags: Attack, Direct Effects: You and the target

title: Dokushin no Jutsu - Poison Truth Technique
text: This technique traps the victim in a state of dream-like hallucination. In that state, the technique's user can try to pry information from them, in the form of questions, which the subject will then (coherently, and audibly) mumble the answer to. Unlike torture, this technique leaves no physical marks, and the victims will not remember what information they revealed or managed to kept secret. text: This technique partially hijacks the victim's nervous system, reacting in response to anything they do and sending conflicting signals. title: Requirements
text: One of the few good things the development of ways to control chakra has brought to the world is the appropriately named medical ninjutsu. These are techniques which safely transfer chakra to another person, or use it to accelerate the natural healing process, cure maladies, and otherwise ameliorate suffering and avoid unnecessary casualties. Medical ninjutsu also has a darker side. The pioneers in the field learned the secrets of the human body so that they could help people, but more than a ha

title: Willing
text: The majority of medical techniques are difficult to be applied to an unwilling participant. These jutsu are listed with the Willing tag to represent them. Any jutsu with this tag will automatically fail against a target who chooses to disrupt it (though you still pay the speed and chakra cost as normal. This can be circumvented against targets that cannot defend themselves such as someone who is unconscious or one trapped with a Nara’s shadow possession.

title: Kyuusho Shuuzen no Jutsu - Vital Repair Technique
text: By transferring your chakra to the recipient, you can stimulate the body to begin the recovery process and help stabilize their most basic functions (like breath rate and pulse). It lacks the precision of more advanced jutsu to target specific injuries and problems, but helps to keep people alive until they can receive advanced care. text: By touching someone and sending pulses of chakra throughout the recipient's tenketsu, the user can learn of someone's vitals and condition faster than it would be to separately evaluate them. It requires the patient to be willing to do so, however, which is the cause of most medic-nin's stress while in training. Chakra: 10 Range: Touch Speed: 10, Delay 10 Requires: Willing Target Tags: Utility Effects: This gives a +5 bonus to any Medicine rolls to treat a person using mundane means (such as a F

title: Shiketsu no Jutsu - Tourniquet Technique
text: A surprisingly medical technique, this throttles the flow of chakra to a specific portion of the body, and by doing so puts it in a state of near-hibernation. The entire limb becomes numb and almost unresponsive, but blood flow decreases and pains is significantly reduced. text: A controlled pulse interrupts pain signals without repairing the underlying injury. The Wound still exists for all other purposes. When the effect ends, that Wound's penalties return immediately. A target may only have one Wound suppressed by this technique at a time.

title: Chakura no Mesu - Chakra Scalpel
text: This forms one's chakra into a small, sharp blade; medics favor this for performing highly accurate incisions during surgeries and dissection, as it won't lose its edge and is always sterile (unlike a regular blade). It can even be used to make cuts inside the body without creating an opening wound, which drastically reduces the risk of infection. Chakra: 13 Upkeep: 3 Speed: 8 Tags: Utility, Self Effects: You can use this in combat. Doing so causes your unarmed taijutsu attacks to inflict Slashi

title: Kasoku Saikassei - Accelerated Revitalization
text: An advanced medical technique which temporarily allows the body to sustain itself by accelerating the body's metabolism and chakra reserves. It was originally developed to extend the medic's usefulness in prolonged missions, but has been expanded since. It is used sparingly because of how long it takes to recover from, and how it tends to leave people comatose afterward. title: Kizu Saishuu no Jutsu - Wound Sealing Technique
text: This technique uses chakra to make repairs to an injured body; gashes are pulled shut, wounds sutured, damaged organs held steady by the application of chakra. This can give an injured shinobi the second wind they need to win a battle or complete a mission. However, this is only a temporary measure; before long the chakra will unravel. title: Meguri Seigyo no Jutsu - Hemostasis Technique
text: Although this technique is fairly simple, it's not taught to amateur medics due to the danger inherent in making any sort of mistake when applying it. This temporarily adjusts the recipient's pulse and blood flow, putting their body in a more stable condition. This is mainly used to prevent someone from bleeding out, and to prevent the spread of poison. text: Weaving a network of chakra, a medic can make short-term repairs to damaged body parts. They can set wounds and hold them rigidly in place, use chakra to take the place of damage muscles and tendons, alleviate swelling and bruising, or even repair damaged blood vessels and do the job of injured nerves. text: Medical knowledge is turned inside out: the user converts carefully prepared chakra and body chemistry into a toxic vapor, then exhales it as a drifting cloud. It is an offensive medical technique precisely because understanding how a body survives also teaches where it fails. Chakra: 30 Range: 15 Area: 6 Speed: 18 Seal Speed: 20 Special: Poison 5 Tags: Attack, AoE, Medical, Environmental Effects: On a failed status Resistance roll, the target suffers Poison 5 for 15 IC. title: Fukugen Ryouhou - Rejuvenating Remedy
text: An advanced technique in which, with a touch, the user sends a pulse of chakra throughout the body of their target, which corrects disruptions in the user's chakra flow and the nerves and blood vessels which they follow throughout the body. It is widely rumored to have been developed by a Hyuuga medic nin. title: Saikan Chuushutsu no Jutsu - Delicate Illness Extraction Technique
text: A delicate and advanced technique even among medical ninjutsu, this is nonetheless exceptionally useful. text: In many ways the pinnacle of medical ninjutsu, this allows the user to dramatically accelerate the body's natural healing process by using chakra to stimulate it. text: A powerful, but potentially dangerous, technique, this allows the medic to transform a portion of their 'life energy' to another individual. Originally, this had no limitations; a medic could easily kill themselves to bring an ally back from the brink of death, which earned the technique its name. title: Requirements
text: Fūinjutsu, or sealing techniques, are, as the name suggests, techniques which use chakra to form specialized 'seals'. They're difficult to use, and have limited combat viability. What makes them useful is that these seals are stable. Normally, any sort of chakra-based effect will expire soon after its user stops applying chakra to it, the energy dissipating back into the world. Seals don't, and depending on the individual seal and the skill of the user some can last for decades if left undisturb

text: The user anchors a thin line of sealing chakra between themselves and a target. title: Introduction
text: Inside the human body there are eight gates which regulate the flow of energy through the person's chakra circulatory system. They have the function of self-imposed biological limiters, preventing a person from catastrophically overexerting themselves. Ninja, however, are nothing if not cheerily self-destructive. Inevitably, shinobi found the way to forcibly, temporarily "open" these gates. The result is a surge of chakra flow through the body, and an accompanying spike in physical performance.

title: Rules
text: When the gates are opened, you have access to a special, second pool of Action Points, starting at 0 and with a maximum of half your normal AP maximum (in other words, AGI/4), called Gate Action Points Pool (GAP Pool). AP provided by the gates (listed under "AP Gain" in their respective entries) goes into your GAP pool. GAP may only be spent on the following things: • Reducing the Speed of taijutsu attacks • Abilities provided by the gates • The ability Principle of Motion • The ability Surge (t

title: Open Gates

Doing this, however, drastically increases the strain put upon your body, causing you to immediately suffer X wounds (as described in Wounding, below). If you are in stealth this reduces your TN by 10 per gate open. For example, if you had three gates open, and wanted to open two more, it would be a Speed (5

title: Close Gates
text: (Speed 5 + 5 \ X) You take several moments to calm yourself and stabilize your chakra flow before willing your chakra gates shut. This shuts all open gates, with X being the number currently opened. Unlike opening, closing them is all-or-nothing.

title: Wounding
text: As mentioned above, using the gates is devastating, in no small part because doing so gives the user's body the ability to physically tear itself apart. Every time you take an action with a Stamina or Chakra cost while using the gates, you have a chance to wound yourself. That chance is: (5 \ (gate opened) + (final speed) + (AP used))% For example, say you had opened the second gate and used a basic unarmed attack (Speed 8), and spent 4 AP to reduce it down to Speed 4. After performing your acti

title: How to Read
text: Each gate contains a brief description of what it does, an "AP Gain" number, and an ability. Every time the IC reaches a multiple of 10, you gain the AP listed under AP Gain, added to your GAP Pool. If that pool is full, any excess AP is simply lost. You only receive the AP Gain of the highest gate you have open. Each gate also has a listed ability, such as the first gate's Enhanced Strength and the second gate's Rejuvenation. You have access to the abilities of all opened gates. For example, wi

title: Restrictions
text: The eight gates work poorly with weapons, much to the woe of many shinobi. This has a great deal to do with their nature: while they grant overwhelming power, the user's technique tends to suffer as a result. Weapons simply aren't meant to be used by a body tearing itself apart, or swung with that sort of speed and force. Additionally, merely having this gate open results in shredding one's muscle fibers.

title: Natural Chakra
text: Natural Chakra is the chakra of the living world: the pressure in the earth, the motion of water, the heat of the air and the life that refuses to die. A shinobi normally produces chakra from within. A Sage learns to become still enough that the world can answer back. Natural Chakra is a Capability Talent built around preparation and balance. You draw Natural Chakra into yourself, enter Sage Mode, then decide when to preserve that balance and when to spend it on Sage Arts.

text: • Natural Chakra is a Capability Talent and requires a valid Source. • Gather Natural Chakra to gain Sage Chakra; stored Sage Chakra is temporary. • Enter Sage Mode once you hold at least 2 Sage Chakra. • Sage Mode improves your combat and senses according to your Sage Rank. • Spend Sage Chakra on Sage Arts and Sage Kata while deciding how long you can maintain the Mode. • Each Deepening raises your Sage Rank and teaches one additional Sage Art or Sage Kata. text: Most shinobi are taught that chakra begins inside the body. Physical and spiritual energy are mixed, shaped through the coils and forced outward into the world. Natural Chakra asks for the opposite instinct. It is already there: in roots pushing through old stone, in rainwater trapped beneath the earth, in the heat rolling over ruined roads and in every living thing stubborn enough to keep growing. A Tortoise Sage may be made to hold a river crossing against impossible weight. A Roc Sage may be abandoned on a cliff with no safe path down. The Source requirement represents earning access to that knowledge in character.
