text: Rocs require space, height and a clear route to move. They can be trained to enter danger for transport or rescue, but deliberate confinement or repeatedly forcing one into a kill-zone with no route out can trigger Rebellion.

title: Serpent Species
text: Role: Control / Poison Serpents are control and counter monsters. They use venom, coils, shedding and patient positioning rather than raw mass.

title: Profile
text: | Toughness | Aggression | Defence | Agility | | 2 | 4 | 4 | 2 | Basic Attack: Speed 10 | Melee | 100% Monster Damage | Piercing Command AP Modifier: +1 Movement: Ground; swims at half Movement

title: Venomous Fangs
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: When the Serpent's Basic Attack fully hits, the target must resist against Monster Save TN. On failure, inflict Poison 1 for 20 IC.

title: Coiling Body
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: The Serpent gains +2 on checks to initiate or maintain Grapples. It may pass through openings a human-sized creature could not, provided its body can physically fit.

title: Constrictor
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: A creature Grappled by the Serpent suffers Immobilization 2. The Serpent's Basic Attacks against a creature it is Grappling deal +15% Final Damage.

title: Shed Skin
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Limit: Once per battle Effects: At the start of the Serpent's Action, end one Grapple, Immobilization, Poison or Burns effect affecting it.

title: King's Coil
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: The Serpent counts as one Size larger for Grapples. Creatures it Grapples suffer -2 Defence, and Venomous Fangs inflicts Poison 2 instead of Poison 1.

title: Potent Venom
text: Type: Stackable Each rank gives +1 to the Resistance TN of Poison inflicted by any Serpent Species Feature or Monster Technique. For every 3 ranks, those Poisons also gain +1 Severity.

title: Flexible Spine
text: Type: Stackable Gain +1 Defence against Grapples, restraints and effects that would forcibly reposition the monster.

title: Scent Tongue
text: Type: Utility The monster can track living creatures by scent and heat traces where plausible, granting +3 to one relevant Survival or Awareness check.

title: Narrow Body
text: Type: Utility The monster can pass through openings and terrain a human-sized creature could not, so long as its body could physically fit; it may carry only what its anatomy reasonably allows.

title: Shed Skin
text: Type: One-Time Shed Skin may also end Paralysis. After using it, the Serpent may move 1 yard without changing Initiative if a legal path exists.

title: Coiling Guard
text: Type: One-Time Gain +2 Parry while Grappling a creature. On a successful Parry while Grappling, the monster may maintain its current Grapple without any additional check caused solely by that Attack.

title: Venom Fang
text: Speed: 10 Base Command AP: 6 Effects: Make an Attack for 90% Monster Damage. On a full hit, the target resists against Monster Save TN; on failure inflict Poison 2 for 20 IC.

title: Coil
text: Speed: 12 Base Command AP: 7 Effects: Make an Attack for 70% Monster Damage. On a hit, attempt a Grapple. While the Grapple is maintained, the target suffers Immobilization 3.

title: Shed Through
text: Speed: 3 Interrupt Base Command AP: 5 Effects: Trigger: the monster is hit by an Attack that would inflict a physical status or restraint. Reduce one inflicted Bleed, Immobilization or Paralysis by 2, minimum 0, after damage resolves.

title: King's Constriction
text: Speed: 14 Base Command AP: 12 Requires: a Grappled target Effects: Attack for 140% Monster Damage as Blunt damage. On a full hit, inflict Suffocation 2 and Immobilization 4 until the Grapple ends.

title: Temperament
text: Serpents are cautious, reciprocal creatures. They respond best to patient handling and consistent signals. Deliberately betraying a trained Serpent's trust or using it to deceive allies it has learned to recognize can trigger Rebellion even when the immediate fight is already won.

title: Tortoise Species
text: Role: Fortress / Protection Tortoises are fortress monsters. They are poor pursuers and weak attackers, but exceptionally difficult to remove and excellent at sheltering allies.

title: Profile
text: | Toughness | Aggression | Defence | Agility | | 5 | 1 | 5 | 1 | Basic Attack: Speed 11 | Melee | 100% Monster Damage | Blunt Command AP Modifier: +2 Movement: Ground; swims at half Movement

title: Living Fortress
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: The Tortoise gains 10 DR. Adjacent allies may treat it as Cover 2 against Attacks originating from the opposite side.

title: Brace
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: If the Tortoise has not voluntarily moved since its previous Action, it gains an additional 5 DR and reduces Knockback suffered by 2, minimum 0.

title: Living Shelter
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: One willing adjacent human-sized ally may ride on the Tortoise's shell. While aboard, that ally moves with the Tortoise without spending Movement to remain with it. Mounting or dismounting is an ordinary object-interaction Action.

title: Bastion
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: Allies using the Tortoise as Cover gain +1 to Defensive Rolls against ranged and Area Attacks when its shell can physically interpose itself.

title: Unbreakable
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: Living Fortress becomes 20 DR and Cover 3. While below half maximum Vitality, the Tortoise gains an additional 5 DR. It cannot be knocked Prone by ordinary forced movement and ignores the first 3 yards of Knockback from each effect.

title: Ancient Shell
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases maximum Vitality by 4% of the monster's unmodified maximum Vitality.

title: Layered Scutes
text: Type: Stackable For every 2 ranks, gain +1 Defence against Attacks originating more than 5 yards away.

title: Living Shelter
text: Type: Utility Outside Initiative, the shell can protect a small group from ordinary rain, wind, falling debris and similar environmental exposure when its size makes that reasonable.

title: Pack Platform
text: Type: Utility The shell may carry one additional human-sized willing creature or equivalent mundane load. This passenger also moves with the Tortoise under Living Shelter.

title: Fortress Shell
text: Type: One-Time While Brace is active, gain an additional 10 DR instead of 5.

title: Sheltering Bulk
text: Type: One-Time Increase the Cover granted by Living Fortress by 1. This makes it Cover 3 before Elder Feature and Cover 4 after Unbreakable.

title: Shell Up
text: Speed: 4 Base Command AP: 4 Effects: Until the monster's next Action, gain +4 Defence and 25 DR, but Movement becomes 0 and it cannot make Attacks.

title: Guardian Shell
text: Speed: 4 Interrupt Base Command AP: 7 Range: 2 yards Effects: Trigger: an adjacent ally is hit by an Attack. The ally gains 20% damage reduction against that Attack as the tortoise interposes its shell.

title: Rolling Bastion
text: Speed: 15 Base Command AP: 8 Effects: Move up to 6 yards in a straight line. Creatures whose spaces are crossed defend against the monster's Accuracy; on failure take 80% Monster Damage and suffer Knockback 3.

title: Mountain That Walks
text: Speed: 17 Base Command AP: 12 Limit: Once per battle Effects: For 20 IC, the monster gains 30 DR and counts as Cover 4. Up to two willing human-sized allies may ride on its shell when this is declared; while they remain aboard, they move with the Tortoise and do not spend movement to remain with it.

title: Temperament
text: Tortoises settle strongly into protective routines. Once trained to shelter a person or position, repeatedly forcing one to abandon that charge to danger without necessity or warning can trigger Rebellion.

title: Gorilla Species
text: Role: Grapple / Utility Gorillas are powerful brawlers and protectors. They excel at climbing, throws, grapples and physically controlling the space around allies.

title: Profile
text: | Toughness | Aggression | Defence | Agility | | 4 | 3 | 4 | 1 | Basic Attack: Speed 11 | Melee | 100% Monster Damage | Blunt Command AP Modifier: +2 Movement: Ground; climbs at half Movement

title: Great Arms
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: The Gorilla gains +2 on Grapple checks and physical checks made to lift, throw, hold or brace a creature or object.

title: Long Arms
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: Increase the Gorilla's melee reach by 1 yard.

title: Hurling Strength
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Speed: 14 Tags: Attack Requires: A Grappled target or unattended object Effects: Throw the target up to 4 yards. A creature takes 60% Monster Damage and lands Prone; an unwilling creature may oppose with Grapple Defence.

title: Protective Instinct
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: Adjacent allies may treat the Gorilla as Cover 1. It gains +3 on checks made to break a Grapple affecting an adjacent ally or pull that ally free.

title: King of the Line
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: The Gorilla counts as one Size larger for Grapples, carrying and forced movement. It may maintain one Grapple with each arm against up to two human-sized creatures. While Grappling only one creature, it gains +2 Defence against forced movement.

title: Great Arms
text: Type: Stackable Each rank gives +1 to Grapple checks and physical checks made to lift, throw, hold or brace a creature or object.

title: Hammering Blows
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases the Basic Attack's Final Damage by 4% against Prone creatures or unattended objects.

title: Climber
text: Type: Utility The monster climbs rough walls, trees and ruins at normal Movement when handholds exist, and gains +3 to Athletics-like physical tasks.

title: Builder's Hands
text: Type: Utility The monster can manipulate ordinary tools, tie ropes, move debris and perform coarse construction despite its size; grant +3 to one relevant Prepare or Survival check.

title: Long Arms
text: Type: One-Time Increase melee reach by 1 additional yard. This stacks with Long Arms.

title: Protective Instinct
text: Type: One-Time Protective Instinct's bonus to break a Grapple affecting an adjacent ally becomes +5, and its Cover increases to Cover 2.

title: Hammerfist
text: Speed: 12 Base Command AP: 6 Effects: Attack for 110% Monster Damage. On a full hit, inflict Knockback 3 or Prone.

title: Hurl
text: Speed: 14 Base Command AP: 8 Requires: a Grappled target or unattended object Effects: Throw it up to 5 yards. A creature takes 80% Monster Damage and lands Prone; an unwilling creature may oppose with Grapple Defence.

title: Grasping Guard
text: Speed: 4 Interrupt Base Command AP: 6 Range: 2 yards Effects: Trigger: an enemy moves past the monster toward an ally. Attempt a Grapple. On success, the triggering movement ends.

title: King's Crash
text: Speed: 16 Base Command AP: 12 Area: 4 yards Effects: The gorilla slams the ground; creatures in Area defend separately. On a hit take 110% Monster Damage and suffer Knockback 4; on a full hit also become Prone.

title: Temperament
text: Gorillas are social, practical and highly responsive to familiar handlers. They work hard when given clear physical tasks, but react poorly to pointless bullying or being made to destroy useful tools, shelter or supplies without purpose.

title: Moth Species
text: Role: Control / Scouting Moths are fragile evasive support monsters. They specialize in flight, dust, concealment, sensory disruption and battlefield utility.

title: Profile
text: | Toughness | Aggression | Defence | Agility | | 1 | 2 | 4 | 5 | Basic Attack: Speed 7 | Melee | 100% Monster Damage | Blunt Command AP Modifier: -2 Movement: Flight

title: Dust Wake
text: Unlock: Core Talent Speed: 8 Area: 3 yards Tags: Utility Effects: Create Visibility 2 in the Area until the Moth's next Action. The Moth ignores Visibility created by its own Species Features.

title: Fluttering Ghost
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: After moving at least 3 yards while airborne, the Moth gains +1 Defence against ranged Attacks until its next Action.

title: Powder Sense
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: The Moth and adjacent allies ignore up to 2 points of Visibility created by the Moth. The Moth also gains +2 Awareness against creatures moving inside its dust.

title: Lulling Dust
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: The first time each hostile creature begins an Action inside Visibility created by the Moth, it must resist against Monster Save TN. On failure, it suffers -2 Awareness until the end of that Action. A creature can be affected once per Moth Action.

title: Moonwing Shroud
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: Dust Wake becomes Area 5 and Visibility 3. When used, choose any number of allies in the Area; those allies ignore that Dust Wake's Visibility.

title: Powdered Wings
text: Type: Stackable For every 2 ranks, increase the Visibility penalty created by Moth Species Features and Monster Techniques by 1.

title: Drifting Flight
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases flying Movement by 0.1 yard per IC.

title: Night Sense
text: Type: Utility The monster ignores up to 4 points of darkness-based Visibility penalty and grants +3 to one Awareness check involving light, vibration or air movement.

title: Pollen Reader
text: Type: Utility The monster can identify disturbed dust, pollen, ash and airborne residue, granting +3 to one Track, Research or Survival check where those traces matter.

title: Soft Landing
text: Type: One-Time The monster and one adjacent willing creature ignore ordinary falling damage from up to 10 yards; greater falls reduce their effective distance by 10 yards.

title: Evasive Flutter
text: Type: One-Time After the Moth successfully Dodges an Attack while airborne, it may move 1 yard without changing Initiative. This cannot happen more than once between its Actions.

title: Dust Veil
text: Speed: 8 Base Command AP: 5 Area: 5 yards Effects: Create Visibility 3 until the monster's next Action. The monster ignores its own Dust Veil.

title: Lulling Powder
text: Speed: 9 Base Command AP: 7 Cone: 5 yards Effects: Targets resist against Monster Save TN. On failure, inflict Paralysis 2 and -2 Awareness for 10 IC.

title: Moonlit Mark
text: Speed: 7 Base Command AP: 5 Range: 15 yards Effects: Dust clings to one creature for 20 IC. That creature cannot benefit from more than 3 points of Visibility against the monster and allies who can see the glowing dust.

title: Wingstorm
text: Speed: 11 Base Command AP: 11 Area: 6 yards Effects: Make an Attack against each hostile creature for 70% Monster Damage and inflict Knockback 3 on a hit. Smoke, loose dust and mundane airborne obscurants in the Area are dispersed.

title: Temperament
text: Moths are curious creatures drawn to light, air currents and strange traces. They are easily distressed by uncontrolled flame and repeated exposure to toxins; deploying one purely to be burned, poisoned or destroyed as a disposable distraction can trigger Rebellion.

title: Beetle Species
text: Role: Siege / Defence Beetles are armoured laborers and siege bodies. They trade speed for carrying power, stubborn defence, burrowing and horn-driven control.

title: Profile
text: | Toughness | Aggression | Defence | Agility | | 5 | 2 | 4 | 1 | Basic Attack: Speed 11 | Melee | 100% Monster Damage | Blunt Command AP Modifier: +2 Movement: Ground

title: Carapace
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: The Beetle gains 10 DR against physical damage.

title: Burrower
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: The Beetle may burrow through ordinary soil and loose earth at half Movement, leaving a crawlable tunnel when the terrain can support it.

title: Horn Drive
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: When the Beetle's Basic Attack fully hits, choose one: inflict Knockback 2, or move the target up to 2 yards to a legal space.

title: Siege Body
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: The Beetle counts as one Size larger for carrying, bracing and forced-movement contests. Its Attacks deal +50% Final Damage against unattended objects, Cover and mundane structures.

title: Immovable Engine
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: Carapace becomes 15 DR against physical damage. The Beetle reduces Knockback suffered by 4, minimum 0, and gains +3 against forced movement. Destroying a mundane obstacle during its movement does not stop that movement if a legal path remains.

title: Carapace Layers
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases maximum Vitality by 4% of the monster's unmodified maximum Vitality.

title: Horn Leverage
text: Type: Stackable For every 2 ranks, increase Knockback or forced movement caused by Beetle Monster Techniques by 1 yard.

title: Burrower
text: Type: Utility Burrower functions at normal Movement instead of half Movement and may also excavate packed ordinary earth when the terrain can support a tunnel.

title: Pack Beast
text: Type: Utility The monster can carry or drag up to two human-sized willing or unconscious creatures, or an equivalent mundane load, without slowing ordinary overland travel.

title: Armoured Underside
text: Type: One-Time Increase the physical DR granted by Carapace by 5.

title: Anchor Claws
text: Type: One-Time Immovable Engine reduces Knockback by an additional 2 and grants an additional +2 against forced movement.

title: Horn Toss
text: Speed: 13 Base Command AP: 7 Effects: Attack for 100% Monster Damage. On a full hit, move the target up to 4 yards and knock it Prone.

title: Burrow Break
text: Speed: 14 Base Command AP: 7 Effects: If standing on diggable ground, the monster burrows and emerges within 6 yards. Its next Basic Attack before the end of the Action gains +2 Accuracy.

title: Carapace Guard
text: Speed: 4 Interrupt Base Command AP: 6 Effects: Trigger: the monster or an adjacent ally is hit by a physical Attack. Reduce Final Damage by 20%; if protecting an ally, the monster takes unreducible Vitality damage equal to half the amount prevented.

title: Siege Horn
text: Speed: 16 Base Command AP: 12 Line: 10 yards Effects: Move through the Line and Attack each creature for 110% Monster Damage. Unattended objects and Cover take +75% Final Damage; a destroyed mundane obstacle does not stop the movement.

title: Temperament
text: Beetles are steady working monsters that respond well to repeated hauling, digging and breaching routines. Needless destruction or constantly abandoning trained tasks halfway through for no reason can make them increasingly difficult to handle.

title: Scorpion Species
text: Role: Control / Poison Scorpions are punishing control monsters with armour, pincers and venomous counterattacks. They are slow but dangerous to approach carelessly.

title: Profile
text: | Toughness | Aggression | Defence | Agility | | 3 | 4 | 4 | 1 | Basic Attack: Speed 11 | Melee | 100% Monster Damage | Piercing Command AP Modifier: +2 Movement: Ground

title: Venom Tail
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: When the Scorpion's Basic Attack fully hits, the target must resist against Monster Save TN. On failure, inflict Poison 1 for 20 IC.

title: Pincer Guard
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: The Scorpion gains +1 Parry against Melee Attacks and +1 on checks to maintain Grapples.

title: Vibration Hunter
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: While touching the same solid ground, the Scorpion can detect moving creatures within 8 yards despite darkness or light concealment. This reveals location and movement, but not identity or detailed information through solid barriers.

title: Retaliatory Sting
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Speed: 4 Interrupt Trigger: The Scorpion successfully Parries a Melee Attack from a creature within reach. Effects: Make an immediate Attack against that creature for 70% Monster Damage. A full hit applies Venom Tail.

title: Deathstalker
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: Venom Tail inflicts Poison 2 instead of Poison 1. When the Scorpion's Basic Attack fully hits a Poisoned creature, it may immediately attempt a Grapple for no Command AP and no additional Speed.

title: Venom Gland
text: Type: Stackable Each rank gives +1 to the Resistance TN of Poison inflicted by any Scorpion Species Feature or Monster Technique. For every 3 ranks, those Poisons also gain +1 Severity.

title: Chitin Plates
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases maximum Vitality by 4% of the monster's unmodified maximum Vitality.

title: Sand Walker
text: Type: Utility Loose sand, scree and shallow rubble do not reduce the monster's Movement, and it can bury itself in loose ground outside Initiative when physically possible.

title: Vibration Sense
text: Type: Utility Vibration Hunter's range increases to 15 yards and grants +3 Awareness when identifying or locating a creature detected through those vibrations.

title: Pincer Guard
text: Type: One-Time Pincer Guard grants +2 Parry and +2 to maintain Grapples instead of +1 to each.

title: Raised Tail
text: Type: One-Time After the monster successfully Parries a Melee Attack, its next Monster Technique against that attacker gains +2 Accuracy before its next Action ends.

title: Venom Sting
text: Speed: 11 Base Command AP: 6 Effects: Attack for 90% Monster Damage. On a full hit, target resists against Monster Save TN; on failure, inflict Poison 2 for 20 IC.

title: Pincer Lock
text: Speed: 13 Base Command AP: 7 Effects: Attack for 70% Monster Damage and attempt a Grapple on hit. While maintained, the target suffers -2 Dodge.

title: Sand Burial
text: Speed: 14 Base Command AP: 7 Requires: loose soil, sand or rubble Effects: Move up to 5 yards underground and emerge; creatures adjacent to the emergence point suffer Immobilization 2 for 10 IC on a failed Defence against the monster's Accuracy.

title: Deathstalker
text: Speed: 15 Base Command AP: 12 Effects: Make two Attacks against one target: a pincer strike for 70% Monster Damage and a sting for 80%. If both hit, the target must resist Poison 4 for 20 IC.

title: Temperament
text: Scorpions are defensive, deliberate and conservative with their venom. They respond poorly to careless handling around allies, pointless attacks on helpless creatures, or repeated commands to waste venom purely for intimidation.

title: Hyena Species
text: Role: Pack Offence / Pursuit Hyenas are relentless opportunists. They thrive on injured prey, morale pressure and repeatedly opening the same target for allies.

title: Profile
text: | Toughness | Aggression | Defence | Agility | | 3 | 4 | 2 | 3 | Basic Attack: Speed 9 | Melee | 100% Monster Damage | Piercing Command AP Modifier: +0 Movement: Ground

title: Pack Opportunist
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: The Hyena's Basic Attacks gain +1 Accuracy against a creature adjacent to one of its allies.

title: Endless Chase
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: Increase the Hyena's Movement by 25% while it moves toward a Wounded or Bleeding creature.

title: Mob Them
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: Once between the Hyena's Actions, when an ally hits a creature within 3 yards of the Hyena, it may move up to 2 yards toward that creature after the Attack resolves without changing Initiative.

title: Cackling Pressure
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: When the Hyena fully hits a creature, that creature suffers -1 Defence against the next Attack made by one of the Hyena's allies before the target's next Action.

title: Feeding Frenzy
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: The Hyena's Basic Attacks against Prone, Wounded or Bleeding creatures deal +25% Final Damage. On a full hit against such a target, it also suffers -2 Defence until its next Action. This does not stack with Cackling Pressure.

title: Bonecracker
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases the Basic Attack's Final Damage by 4% against a target that has suffered a Wound this scene.

title: Endless Chase
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases Movement by 0.1 yard per IC while moving toward a Wounded or Bleeding enemy.

title: Carrion Wise
text: Type: Utility Grant +3 to Survival or Research checks involving carcasses, scavengers, feeding sites, disease signs or determining whether remains were disturbed.

title: Laughing Signal
text: Type: Utility The monster can coordinate simple warnings and directions over long distances by distinctive calls; allies familiar with it can distinguish danger, retreat, found trail and rally signals.

title: Pack Opportunist
text: Type: One-Time Pack Opportunist grants +2 Accuracy instead of +1, and Basic Attacks benefiting from it deal +10% Final Damage.

title: Unnerving Cackle
text: Type: One-Time Enemies within 5 yards suffer -2 to Resistance against fear-based effects created by the monster.

title: Cackling Feint
text: Speed: 9 Base Command AP: 5 Range: 8 yards Effects: One target resists against Monster Save TN. On failure it suffers -2 Defence against the next Attack made against it before its next Action. This is a fear-based effect.

title: Harrier Bite
text: Speed: 10 Base Command AP: 6 Effects: Attack for 105% Monster Damage. If an ally hit the target since the monster's previous Action, gain +2 Accuracy.

title: Bonecrush
text: Speed: 12 Base Command AP: 9 Effects: Attack for 130% Monster Damage. Against a Prone or Wounded target, increase damage to 150%.

title: Feeding Frenzy
text: Speed: 13 Base Command AP: 12 Effects: Make an Attack for 100% Monster Damage. If it hits, up to two allies within 3 yards may each move 2 yards toward the target without changing Initiative. The target suffers -2 Defence until its next Action.

title: Temperament
text: Hyenas are food-motivated pack hunters and learn quickly through shared hunts and consistent reward. Starving one of expected rewards, isolating it from familiar packmates without cause, or repeatedly wasting kills after encouraging it to hunt can trigger Rebellion.

title: Elk Species
text: Role: Escort / Mobility Elk are mobile guides and protective escorts. They excel at travel, terrain crossing, carrying allies and using antlers to redirect danger.

title: Profile
text: | Toughness | Aggression | Defence | Agility | | 3 | 2 | 3 | 4 | Basic Attack: Speed 8 | Melee | 100% Monster Damage | Blunt Command AP Modifier: -1 Movement: Ground

title: Sure-Footed Guide
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: The Elk ignores mundane Movement penalties from shallow snow, mud, roots, undergrowth and steep natural slopes where a hoofed animal could reasonably pass. It may carry one willing human-sized rider at half Movement.

title: Antler Catch
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: After successfully Parrying a Melee Attack, the Elk may move the attacker 1 yard to either side of itself if a legal space exists.

title: Escort Step
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: When the Elk takes a Move Action, one willing adjacent ally may move up to half the distance the Elk moved after it finishes, without changing that ally's Initiative. The ally must follow a legal path and end within 2 yards of the Elk.

title: Protective Herd
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: The Elk's rider and allies within 2 yards gain +1 Defence against Melee Attacks and forced-movement effects while the Elk is conscious and able to move.

title: Great Crossing
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: The Elk may carry up to two willing human-sized allies at full Movement. It ignores mundane Difficult Terrain and may cross ordinary gaps up to 2 yards without a check when a physically plausible landing exists.

title: Long Stride
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases Movement by 0.1 yard per IC.

title: Branching Guard
text: Type: Stackable For every 2 ranks, gain +1 Parry against Melee Attacks made by creatures that moved at least 3 yards before attacking.

title: Wayfinder
text: Type: Utility Grant +3 to Survival checks for navigation, weather sense, finding safe trails or selecting an overland route.

title: Sure-Footed
text: Type: Utility Sure-Footed Guide also grants +3 Defence against forced movement and effects that would knock the Elk Prone while standing on natural terrain.

title: Rider
text: Type: One-Time The Elk may carry one additional human-sized willing rider. Before Great Crossing, carrying the additional rider reduces Movement by half; Great Crossing removes this penalty.

title: Antler Catch
text: Type: One-Time Antler Catch also grants +2 Parry against Melee Attacks made by creatures that moved at least 3 yards immediately before attacking.

title: Antler Guard
text: Speed: 4 Interrupt Base Command AP: 6 Range: 2 yards Effects: Trigger: an ally is targeted by a Melee Attack. The elk moves up to 2 yards and Parries on that ally's behalf if it can interpose its antlers.

title: Trailblazer
text: Speed: 9 Base Command AP: 5 Effects: The elk and one adjacent willing ally move up to 6 yards. That movement ignores mundane Difficult Terrain.

title: Stampede Line
text: Speed: 11 Base Command AP: 9 Line: 10 yards Effects: Move along the Line and Attack creatures in it for 90% Monster Damage. On a hit, inflict Knockback 4.

title: Great Crossing
text: Speed: 12 Base Command AP: 11 Effects: The elk moves up to twice its normal Movement and may carry up to two willing human-sized allies during this movement. It can cross ordinary gaps, shallow water and rough natural terrain without checks if a physically plausible route exists.

title: Temperament
text: Elk are herd-minded, route-oriented monsters that settle best with familiar trails and calm handling. Needless destruction of habitat, slaughter around them, or repeatedly forcing them to trample safe ground without purpose can trigger Rebellion.

title: Wyrm Species
text: Role: Elemental / Bruiser Wyrms are hardy draconic generalists. They combine scales, unusual movement and a chosen breath affinity, but lack the extreme specialization of other species.

title: Profile
text: | Toughness | Aggression | Defence | Agility | | 4 | 3 | 2 | 3 | Basic Attack: Speed 9 | Melee | 100% Monster Damage | Slashing Command AP Modifier: +0 Movement: Ground

title: Lesser Breath
text: Unlock: Core Talent Speed: 11 Cone: 4 yards Tags: Attack, Energy Effects: When the monster is acquired, choose Fire, Water, Wind, Earth or Lightning as the Wyrm's Breath Affinity. Attack each creature in the Cone for 60% Monster Damage as Energy damage. Lesser Breath carries the chosen elemental tag and is an Independent Action.

title: Scale Ward
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: The Wyrm gains 15% damage reduction against effects carrying its Breath Affinity's elemental tag and +2 Defence against Attacks carrying that tag.

title: Draconic Movement
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: Choose one: Burrow through ordinary soil at half Movement, or Glide to ignore ordinary falling damage. If another rule already grants the chosen option, improve it as that rule describes instead.

title: Greater Breath
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: Lesser Breath becomes Cone 6 and deals 80% Monster Damage. On a full hit, apply the Breath Affinity's rider: Fire inflicts Burns 1; Water inflicts Knockback 1; Wind inflicts Knockback 2; Earth inflicts Immobilization 1; Lightning inflicts Paralysis 1.

title: Winged Elder
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: The Wyrm gains true flight at half normal Movement. Lesser Breath now deals 100% Monster Damage while retaining Greater Breath's Cone and elemental rider.

title: Thick Scales
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases maximum Vitality by 4% of the monster's unmodified maximum Vitality.

title: Deep Breath
text: Type: Stackable For every 2 ranks, increase the Range, Line or Cone size of Wyrm Breath Species Features and Monster Techniques by 1 yard.

title: Elemental Scent
text: Type: Utility Choose Fire, Water, Wind, Earth or Lightning when selected. Grant +3 to Awareness or Research checks to identify recent physical traces of that element or its chakra effects. May be selected again for another element.

title: Burrow or Glide
text: Type: Utility Choose one improvement: gain the Draconic Movement option you do not possess, improve Burrow to normal Movement, or allow Glide to travel up to 2 horizontal yards for every 1 yard descended. This Utility Trait may be selected again for a different improvement.

title: Breath Affinity
text: Type: One-Time The Wyrm's chosen Breath Affinity becomes especially potent. Increase any numerical Burns, Knockback, Immobilization or Paralysis rider caused by its Breath Species Features and Monster Techniques by 1, and gain +2 Resistance against environmental effects of that element.

title: Winged Wyrm
text: Type: One-Time If Winged Elder is not yet unlocked, gain true flight at half normal Movement and require the Glide option from Draconic Movement or Burrow or Glide. Once Winged Elder is unlocked, flying Movement becomes normal Movement instead.

title: Wyrm Breath
text: Speed: 11 Base Command AP: 7 Line: 8 yards Effects: Attack each creature in the Line for 100% Monster Damage as Energy damage carrying the Wyrm's Breath Affinity elemental tag. On a full hit: Fire inflicts Burns 1; Water inflicts Knockback 1; Wind inflicts Knockback 2; Earth inflicts Immobilization 1; Lightning inflicts Paralysis 1.

title: Scale Ward
text: Speed: 4 Interrupt Base Command AP: 6 Effects: Trigger: the monster is hit. Reduce Final Damage by 20% and gain +2 Defence until its next Action against attacks sharing the Breath Affinity's element.

title: Coiling Rush
text: Speed: 11 Base Command AP: 7 Effects: Move up to 5 yards and Attack for 105% Monster Damage. On a full hit, inflict Knockback 3 or Prone.

title: Elder Breath
text: Speed: 14 Base Command AP: 12 Effects: Line 12 or Cone 7, chosen when used. Attack each target for 115% Monster Damage as Energy damage. If the Wyrm has Breath Affinity, the technique carries that elemental tag. On a full hit: Fire inflicts Burns 2; Water inflicts Knockback 2; Wind inflicts Knockback 3; Earth inflicts Immobilization 2; Lightning inflicts Paralysis 2.

title: Temperament
text: Wyrms are proud, territorial and highly intelligent monsters. They respond best to confident handlers and a stable den or territory. Humiliating treatment, using one as a trophy, or repeatedly violating established training boundaries can trigger Rebellion.

title: Leech Species
text: Role: Sustain / Support Leeches are sustain monsters. They cling, drain, transfer vitality and purge harmful substances rather than winning through direct offence.

title: Profile
text: | Toughness | Aggression | Defence | Agility | | 4 | 2 | 3 | 3 | Basic Attack: Speed 9 | Melee | 100% Monster Damage | Piercing Command AP Modifier: +0 Movement: Ground; swims at normal Movement

title: Blood Feeder
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: When the Leech's Basic Attack deals damage, it restores Vitality equal to 15% of Final Damage dealt, up to 5% of its maximum Vitality per Action.

title: Clinging Body
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: The Leech gains +2 on checks to maintain Grapples. It may remain attached to a willing creature without impeding that creature's Movement.

title: Filter Feeder
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: The Leech gains +2 Resistance against Poison and disease-like biological effects. While attached to a willing creature, that creature also gains +2 Resistance against those effects.

title: Purging Bite
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Speed: 10 Range: Touch Tags: Utility Effects: Touch a willing creature and reduce one Poison, Burns or Bleed status by 1, minimum 0. The Leech loses Vitality equal to 5% of its maximum.

title: Red Feast
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: Blood Feeder restores Vitality equal to 30% of Final Damage dealt, up to 10% of maximum Vitality per Action. Whenever Blood Feeder restores Vitality, one adjacent or attached living ally also restores HP equal to half the amount restored, to a maximum of 5% of the Leech's maximum Vitality per Action.

title: Blood Reservoir
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases maximum Vitality by 4% of the monster's unmodified maximum Vitality.

title: Efficient Feeder
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases Vitality restored by Leech Species Features and Monster Techniques by 4%.

title: Toxin Taster
text: Type: Utility The monster can detect whether a touched liquid, wound or food contains an obvious biological poison or contaminant, granting +3 to a relevant Medicine or Toxicology check.

title: Medicinal Saliva
text: Type: Utility When the monster assists mundane wound treatment outside Initiative, grant +3 to one Medicine check. It cannot replace required tools or medical jutsu.

title: Clinging Body
text: Type: One-Time Clinging Body's bonus to maintain Grapples becomes +3. While attached to a willing creature, forced movement affecting that creature does not automatically detach the Leech.

title: Filter Feeder
text: Type: One-Time Filter Feeder's Resistance bonus becomes +5 for the Leech and +3 for a willing creature it is attached to.

title: Blood Draw
text: Speed: 10 Base Command AP: 6 Effects: Attack for 80% Monster Damage. On hit, restore Vitality to the monster equal to 25% of Final Damage dealt, up to 10% of its maximum Vitality.

title: Transfusion
text: Speed: 11 Base Command AP: 7 Range: 0 yards Effects: Transfer up to 15% of the monster's current Vitality to an adjacent living ally as restored Vitality. This cannot restore HP or repair Wounds.

title: Purge
text: Speed: 12 Base Command AP: 8 Range: 0 yards Effects: Touch a willing creature. Reduce one Poison, Burns or Bleed status by 2, minimum 0. The monster loses Vitality equal to 5% of its maximum per level removed.

title: Red Feast
text: Speed: 13 Base Command AP: 12 Effects: Attack for 120% Monster Damage. Restore Vitality equal to 40% of Final Damage dealt, then distribute that restored amount between the monster and one adjacent ally. Once per battle.

title: Temperament
text: Leeches treat blood as food and respond strongly to feeding routines. They can be trained to drain enemies and aid familiar allies, but deliberately feeding one on helpless allies for cruelty, spectacle or convenience can trigger Rebellion.

title: Crab Species
text: Role: Defence / Grapple Crabs are defensive controllers. Their shell and pincers dominate narrow spaces, punish movement and hold targets in place.

title: Profile
text: | Toughness | Aggression | Defence | Agility | | 4 | 2 | 5 | 1 | Basic Attack: Speed 11 | Melee | 100% Monster Damage | Blunt Command AP Modifier: +2 Movement: Ground

title: Shell Wall
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: The Crab gains 10 DR against physical damage. An adjacent ally may treat it as Cover 1 against Attacks originating from the opposite side.

title: Vice Grip
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: The Crab gains +1 on checks to initiate or maintain a Grapple with its pincers. When its Basic Attack hits by 5 or more, it may immediately attempt a Grapple for no Command AP and no additional Speed.

title: Amphibious
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: Shallow water, surf and seabeds do not impose mundane Movement penalties on the Crab. It may swim at half normal Movement and remain underwater for an entire scene without Suffocation checks.

title: Sideways Guard
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: After successfully Dodging an Attack, the Crab may move 1 yard without changing Initiative. This can occur once between its Actions.

title: Control Zone
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Speed: 4 Interrupt Trigger: A hostile creature voluntarily leaves the Crab's melee reach. Effects: Attempt a Grapple. On success, the triggering movement ends. Shell Wall also becomes 15 DR against physical damage and Cover 2, and the Crab reduces Knockback suffered by 2, minimum 0.

title: Shell Layers
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases maximum Vitality by 4% of the monster's unmodified maximum Vitality.

title: Vice Grip
text: Type: Stackable For every 2 ranks, gain +1 on checks to initiate or maintain a Grapple with the pincers.

title: Amphibious
text: Type: Utility Amphibious improves the Crab's swimming Movement from half to full normal Movement and grants +3 on checks to resist currents or aquatic forced movement.

title: Burrowing Crab
text: Type: Utility Outside Initiative, the monster can dig shallow pits, trenches or hiding hollows in sand or loose soil at half normal working time.

title: Sideways Guard
text: Type: One-Time Sideways Guard may move 2 yards instead of 1 after a successful Dodge.

title: Wall of Shell
text: Type: One-Time Increase the Cover granted by Shell Wall by 1. This makes it Cover 2 before Elder Feature and Cover 3 after Control Zone.

title: Pincer Hold
text: Speed: 12 Base Command AP: 7 Effects: Attack for 80% Monster Damage and attempt a Grapple on hit. A target Grappled this way suffers -2 to actions that require the held limb.

title: Shell Wall
text: Speed: 4 Base Command AP: 5 Effects: Until the monster's next Action, gain +3 Defence and become Cover 3, but Movement is halved.

title: Undertow
text: Speed: 13 Base Command AP: 7 Requires: water or loose sand Effects: Attack a creature within 5 yards for 70% Monster Damage; on hit pull it 4 yards toward the crab.

title: Crushing Clamp
text: Speed: 15 Base Command AP: 11 Requires: a Grappled target Effects: Attack for 140% Monster Damage. On a full hit, inflict Immobilization 4 until the Grapple ends.

title: Temperament
text: Crabs are territorial and settle quickly into guarding a chosen space. They will hold that space under heavy pressure, but repeatedly forcing one to abandon creatures or positions it has been trained to shelter can trigger Rebellion.

title: Hound Species
text: Role: Tracking / Teamwork Hounds are reliable hunting partners. They specialize in scent, teamwork, takedowns and protecting the person they have accepted as their handler.

title: Profile
text: | Toughness | Aggression | Defence | Agility | | 3 | 3 | 2 | 4 | Basic Attack: Speed 8 | Melee | 100% Monster Damage | Piercing Command AP Modifier: -1 Movement: Ground

title: Tracking Hound
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: A meaningful scent sample such as blood, clothing or fur lets the Hound establish a physical trail where one plausibly remains. It gains +3 Survival when following that trail.

title: Handler's Guard
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: While within 2 yards of you, the Hound gains +1 Defence and you gain +1 Defence against Melee Attacks.

title: Takedown Bite
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: When the Hound's Basic Attack hits by 5 or more, choose one: knock the target Prone, or immediately attempt a Grapple. This costs no Command AP and adds no Speed.

title: Handler Guard
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Speed: 4 Interrupt Trigger: You are hit by a Melee Attack. Effects: The Hound may move up to 3 yards toward you. If it becomes adjacent, reduce that Attack's Final Damage by 10%.

title: Perfect Teamwork
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: When you fully hit a creature, the Hound's next Basic Attack against it before the end of its next Action gains +2 Accuracy and +20% Final Damage. When the Hound fully hits a creature, your next Attack against it before the end of your next Action gains +1 Accuracy. Neither benefit stacks with itself.

title: Keen Nose
text: Type: Stackable Gain +1 on Survival or Awareness checks that rely on scent.

title: Pack Pressure
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases the Basic Attack's Final Damage by 4% against a creature adjacent to one of the monster's allies.

title: Tracking Hound
text: Type: Utility Tracking Hound grants +5 Survival instead of +3. When the Hound successfully locates a Hidden creature by scent, it may immediately Point Out that creature.

title: Working Dog
text: Type: Utility Choose one of Awareness, Espionage, Survival or Athletics. When the hound meaningfully assists that kind of task, grant +3 to the allied check. This Utility Trait may be selected again for another skill.

title: Handler's Guard
text: Type: One-Time Handler's Guard grants the Hound +2 Defence instead of +1. The tamer's +1 Defence remains unchanged.

title: Takedown Bite
text: Type: One-Time When Takedown Bite triggers, the Hound may both knock the target Prone and immediately attempt the Grapple instead of choosing one.

title: Tracking Fang
text: Speed: 10 Base Command AP: 6 Requires: a meaningful scent trail Effects: The hound may pursue a target it cannot currently see along a plausible physical route, gaining +5 Survival and immediately Pointing Out the target if it locates them in Stealth.

title: Takedown
text: Speed: 9 Base Command AP: 7 Effects: Attack for 90% Monster Damage. On a hit by 5 or more, knock the target Prone and attempt a Grapple.

title: Handler Guard
text: Speed: 4 Interrupt Base Command AP: 6 Range: 3 yards Effects: Trigger: the tamer is hit by a Melee Attack. The hound moves up to 3 yards toward them; if it becomes adjacent, reduce that Attack's Final Damage by 20%.

title: Pack Hunt
text: Speed: 12 Base Command AP: 11 Effects: Attack for 120% Monster Damage. If at least one ally is adjacent to the target, gain +2 Accuracy; on a full hit, that ally may move 2 yards without changing Initiative.

title: Temperament
text: Hounds are strongly handler-focused and thrive on familiar routines, work and pack contact. Deliberate abandonment, disposable use, or knowingly sending one to die simply to save the tamer effort can trigger Rebellion.

title: Panther Species
text: Role: Stealth / Assault Panthers are extreme offensive hunters. They are accurate, fast and lethal from concealment, but their poor Defence makes bad positioning costly.

title: Profile
text: | Toughness | Aggression | Defence | Agility | | 2 | 5 | 1 | 4 | Basic Attack: Speed 8 | Melee | 100% Monster Damage | Slashing Command AP Modifier: -1 Movement: Ground; climbs at half Movement

title: Silent Predator
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: The Panther gains +2 on Stealth checks involving stalking or ambushes. Its Basic Attacks made while Hidden or from Cover gain +1 Accuracy.

title: Pounce
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: If the Panther moves at least 4 yards directly toward a target before making a Basic Attack, a full hit also knocks that target Prone.

title: Fade After Blood
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: After the Panther fully hits with a Basic Attack while it began the Action Hidden or behind Cover, it may move 1 yard without changing Initiative. This can occur once per Panther Action.

title: Ambush Killer
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: The Panther's Basic Attacks made while Hidden or from Cover deal +20% Final Damage.

title: Apex Stalker
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Limit: Once per battle Effects: The Panther's first Attack against a creature that has not detected it gains +3 Accuracy and +25% Final Damage. On a full hit, inflict Bleed 3. After the Attack resolves, the Panther may move up to 3 yards toward legal Cover without changing Initiative.

title: Killing Claws
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases the Basic Attack's Final Damage by 4% when made from Stealth, Cover, or after moving at least 5 yards.

title: Predator's Focus
text: Type: Stackable For every 2 ranks, gain +1 Accuracy with the Basic Attack against a target that has not yet acted since the Panther's previous Action.

title: Silent Paws
text: Type: Utility Grant +3 to Stealth checks involving stalking, moving quietly or preparing an ambush with the panther.

title: Night Hunter
text: Type: Utility Ignore up to 4 points of darkness-based Visibility penalty for Awareness and movement.

title: Pounce
text: Type: One-Time When Pounce triggers, the Basic Attack also deals +10% Final Damage.

title: Fade After Blood
text: Type: One-Time Fade After Blood may move 2 yards instead of 1. If that movement ends in legal Cover or concealment, the Panther may immediately attempt to Hide.

title: Shadow Pounce
text: Speed: 8 Base Command AP: 7 Effects: Move up to 6 yards and Attack for 110% Monster Damage. If the Panther began the Action Hidden or behind Cover, gain +2 Accuracy.

title: Throat Claw
text: Speed: 10 Base Command AP: 8 Effects: Attack for 125% Monster Damage. If the target is Prone, Grappled, or has not detected the Panther, increase this to 150% Monster Damage.

title: Vanish Between Blows
text: Speed: 4 Base Command AP: 6 Effects: Move up to 4 yards to Cover or concealment and immediately attempt to Hide if the normal conditions for Hide are met. This Action does not by itself break existing Stealth.

title: Nightfall Kill
text: Speed: 12 Base Command AP: 12 Effects: Make an Attack for 160% Monster Damage at -2 Accuracy. If the Panther began this Action Hidden, remove the Accuracy penalty. On a full hit, inflict Bleed 4.

title: Temperament
text: Panthers value autonomy, patience and a clean hunt. They object to confinement, humiliating busywork, and pointless cruelty. A trained Panther may be aloof, but responds well to clear purpose, room to stalk, and handlers who do not waste its effort.

title: Medical Training
text: Medical Ninjutsu requires a level of Chakra control and anatomical knowledge that most Hunters never need. A trained medic is not simply someone who can restore HP; they are the person who can look at a body falling apart and know which failure matters first.

title: Core Talent
text: You may learn D- and C-Rank Medical Ninjutsu. You also gain Triage: Speed 5, Utility, Touch Triage — Examine a willing, helpless, or unconscious living creature. Learn its current HP category, Fatigue Level, and the severity and location of any physical Wounds you could reasonably diagnose. This does not automatically reveal curses, poisons, hidden seals, or supernatural conditions that require their own checks.

title: Developments
text: Combat Medic — When one of your Medical Ninjutsu restores HP to an ally during battle, that ally may either remove 2 Stun or regain 1 AP, up to their normal maximum. Anatomist — After successfully using Triage or a Medicine check to examine a living creature, gain +2 Accuracy on your next Attack against that creature before the end of the scene. This represents anatomical knowledge and does not apply when the creature's anatomy is completely alien to what you examined. Chakra Surgeon — Gain acce

title: Mastery
text: Surgeon of the Corps — Gain access to A-Rank Medical Ninjutsu if you otherwise meet their normal requirements. In addition, once per battle when you successfully stabilize or restore HP to a character at 0 HP, they may immediately ignore the numerical penalties of one physical Wound until the end of their next Action. The Wound is not removed.

title: Natural Chakra
text: Natural Chakra is the chakra of the living world. A shinobi normally produces chakra from within; a Sage learns to draw balanced Natural Chakra from the world around them.

title: Core Talent
text: Choose a Sage Tradition from a creature, Summon Tribe or other valid Source capable of teaching Natural Chakra. Gain Sage Rank 1, a maximum Sage Chakra of 4, Gather Natural Chakra, Sage Mode, your Tradition's Signature Trait, and one Sage Art or Sage Kata you meet the requirements for.

title: Developments
text: Natural Chakra uses Sage Arts and Sage Kata as its Developments. Each time you Deepen this Talent, increase your Sage Rank by 1 and learn one additional Sage Art or Sage Kata you qualify for; the selected Art or Kata is that Development. The Art or Kata granted by the Core Talent is not a Development. You may Deepen Natural Chakra up to four times, to a maximum Sage Rank of 5. Mastery is gained after the third Development as normal; the fourth Deepening remains available after Mastery and still

title: Mastery
text: Perfect Communion — After three Natural Chakra Developments, reduce Gather Natural Chakra's base Speed by 1 and its minimum Speed by 1. Reduce Sage Mode's Upkeep by 1, minimum 0. The first time you enter Sage Mode in each battle, gain 1 Sage Chakra after Sage Mode resolves, up to your maximum.

title: Exotic Venoms
text: Most poisoners work with substances a competent field medic has seen before. You have learned to find, preserve, identify, and weaponize things that should never have been put in a bottle.

title: Core Talent
text: You may acquire, harvest, craft, and use Exotic Venoms permitted by the Equipment and Crafting rules. Once per Hunt, when a defeated or studied creature could reasonably provide a venom, toxin, poisonous organ, paralytic secretion, or similar component, you may identify one additional toxin reagent that can be recovered from it. This reagent is still subject to normal harvesting and crafting requirements. You also gain Identify Toxin: Speed 5, Utility Identify Toxin — Examine a poison, poisoned

title: Developments
text: Toxicologist — Gain +5 Medicine on checks made specifically to identify, treat, or create antidotes for poisons and venoms you have encountered before. Rapid Application — Actions used specifically to apply a poison to a weapon, tool, trap, or prepared delivery system have their final Speed reduced by 3, minimum 1. Refined Dose — Poisons you personally prepare impose +2 to the relevant Resistance TN, if they use one. A creature cannot suffer this bonus from more than one of your doses at a time.

title: Mastery
text: Signature Toxin — During a Week's Rest, you may designate one poison you personally create as your Signature Toxin. Until your next Week's Rest, its relevant Resistance TN increases by an additional +1 and any numerical duration it has increases by 20%, rounding down. You may only maintain one Signature Toxin formula at a time.

title: Seal Training
text: Fūinjutsu is less about handseals than it is about understanding Chakra as language: boundaries, conditions, storage, suppression, and instructions written into the world.

title: Core Talent
text: You may learn C- and B-Rank Sealing Ninjutsu. During each Week's Rest, choose one Sealing Ninjutsu you know as a Prepared Formula. The first time you use that technique before your next Week's Rest, reduce its final Seal Speed by 2 and its final Action Speed by 2, minimum 1. You may only have one Prepared Formula at a time unless a Development increases this limit.

title: Developments
text: Combat Scribe — All Sealing Ninjutsu you perform have their final Seal Speed reduced by 2, minimum 0. Barrier Specialist — Gain +2 on Attack, Defense, or Skill rolls made specifically to establish, reinforce, contest, or repair a sealing barrier. If the barrier does not use such a roll, gain +10% to any HP or durability the barrier receives from your own stats, rounding down. Suppression Specialist — Gain +2 Accuracy on Sealing Ninjutsu used specifically to suppress, bind, contain, or interfere

title: Mastery
text: Grand Formula — Gain access to A-Rank Sealing Ninjutsu if you otherwise meet their normal requirements. During each Week's Rest, choose one of your Prepared Formulae as a Grand Formula. Its first use before your next Week's Rest reduces final Seal Speed by 5 and final Action Speed by 2, minimum 1, instead of the normal Prepared Formula reduction.

title: Master Artisan
text: A Master Artisan understands that the difference between scrap and treasure is often whether anyone present knows what they are looking at. At this level, materials other craftsmen treat as dangerous curiosities become ingredients.

title: Core Talent
text: Choose mastery of two Wondrous Materials from the current list: Skysteel, Ironheart, Angelskin, Crypstone, Mindglass, Voidglass, Feathersteel, Deepstone, Echo Brass, Shiversteel, Living Wood, Prismite, Anchorite, Ghostsilver, Bloodglass, Stormsilver, Black Jade, and Phaseglass. You may use their special properties when crafting weapons or other equipment as permitted by the Crafting rules.

title: Developments
text: Material Savant — Master two additional Wondrous Materials from the available list. Monsterwright — Gain +5 on Crafting checks where a meaningful Trophy or monster component is one of the primary materials. You may also identify whether a recovered monster component is suitable for weapon, armor, tool, pharmaceutical, or seal work without needing a separate Downtime action if the answer would be apparent to an expert. Efficient Workshop — Reduce the time required for your ordinary Crafting Downt

title: Mastery
text: Magnum Opus — You may work with every Wondrous Material currently available to ordinary Master Artisans. You may also maintain one Magnum Opus: a permanent item you personally crafted which may support one additional minor special property when the Crafting rules and its materials could reasonably support that property. Creating or changing your Magnum Opus still requires the normal materials, Downtime, and crafting rolls.

title: Elemental Mastery
text: Most shinobi learn an element as a language. You have spent enough time with one nature that it has become an accent in everything you do.

title: Core Talent
text: Choose one standard elemental affinity you possess: Katon, Fūton, Raiton, Doton, or Suiton. This choice is permanent. When declaring a Ninjutsu with your chosen element, choose one Elemental Control: Efficient Moulding — Reduce its Chakra cost by 3, minimum 1. Clean Release — Reduce its final Seal Speed by 2, minimum 0.

title: Developments
text: Elemental Precision — Attacks using your chosen element gain +1 Accuracy. Efficient Nature — Efficient Moulding reduces Chakra cost by 5 instead of 3. Rapid Weaving — Clean Release reduces final Seal Speed by 4 instead of 2. Elemental Counter — Gain +2 on Defensive Rolls made against techniques of your chosen element. After you successfully Defend against one, your next Attack using your chosen element gains +1 Accuracy. Environmental Conduit — When a technique of your chosen element can meaning

title: Mastery
text: True Nature — When using Elemental Control, apply both Efficient Moulding and Clean Release to the same technique. If both would already apply from another rule, instead gain +1 Accuracy on that technique.

title: Interrogator
text: Some people crack under threats. Others talk because somebody made them comfortable. The useful skill is knowing which person is sitting in front of you before you choose the tool.

title: Core Talent
text: You gain Read the Subject: Speed 10, Utility, Social Read the Subject — After at least a brief meaningful exchange with a creature capable of communicating with you, make an Espionage check opposed by their Espionage or another appropriate defensive social roll. On success, choose one: Learn whether they are deliberately withholding something relevant to the current subject. Identify the person, topic, place, or consequence that produces the strongest visible emotional reaction during the exchan

title: Developments
text: Rapport — Gain +3 Espionage when gathering information from a willing, cooperative, or conversational target rather than threatening or restraining them. Pressure — Once per scene, after a target refuses to answer, deliberately evades a question, or ends an exchange, you may immediately make another Read the Subject check against them with +3. Cross-Examination — When a target contradicts something they previously told you during the same scene, gain +5 on your next Read the Subject check agains

title: Mastery
text: Break the Story — Once per scene, after you have succeeded on at least two Read the Subject checks against the same target, you may ask one direct question. The target is never compelled to answer. If they answer, you automatically recognize whether the response is a deliberate lie, a deliberate evasion, or something they sincerely believe. This does not reveal what the truth actually is. Against another player character, use this only when the normal social/PvP rules permit such information to

title: Weapon Savant
text: A weapon stops being equipment after enough years in your hands. Its weight becomes posture, its reach becomes distance, and the space around you starts being measured in cuts.

title: Core Talent
text: Choose one weapon family or closely related group of weapons you are proficient with. The choice should describe one coherent fighting discipline, such as swords, spears, axes, bows, staves, or thrown weapons, rather than all melee or all ranged weapons. Attacks made with your chosen weapon family gain +1 Accuracy.

title: Developments
text: Guard Mastery — Gain +2 to Take the Hit and Parry rolls with your chosen weapon Quick Draw — The first Attack you declare after drawing, readying, or switching to a weapon from your chosen family has its final Speed reduced by 2, minimum 1. Tempo — After successfully Blocking or Parrying with your chosen weapon family, reduce the final Speed of your next Attack with that weapon family by 2, minimum 1. Weapon Control — Gain +3 on rolls made specifically to Disarm, bind, trap, contest, or otherwis

title: Mastery
text: Extension of the Body — When declaring an Attack with your chosen weapon family, choose one: gain +3 Accuracy, or reduce the Attack's final Speed by 3, minimum 1. Declare the choice before rolling.

title: Sensor Training
text: Most Hunters use their eyes until the world gives them a reason not to. Sensors learn to feel Chakra itself: presence, motion, pressure, and the faint signatures left behind when somebody thought they were gone.

title: Core Talent
text: You gain Chakra Sense: Speed 10, Chakra 5, Utility, Concentration Chakra Sense — Until the end of your next Action, you can sense unsuppressed Chakra sources within 30 yards even without line of sight, unless a barrier or effect specifically blocks Chakra sensing. You learn the number of distinct sources you can sense and their rough direction. This does not automatically reveal identity, exact position, elemental affinities, techniques, or whether a source is hostile. When a creature is deliber

title: Developments
text: Wide Field — Increase Chakra Sense range to 100 yards. Beyond 30 yards you learn only the number and broad direction of signatures unless another Development says otherwise. Signature Memory — After sensing the same creature for at least 20 IC or spending meaningful time around them, you may memorize their Chakra signature. Gain +5 on later Chakra Control rolls made specifically to recognize that creature by Chakra. You may retain a number of memorized signatures equal to 3 + XP/1000; replacing

title: Mastery
text: Mind's Eye — While conscious, you passively sense unsuppressed Chakra sources within 15 yards without activating Chakra Sense or paying its Chakra cost. You learn only presence and rough direction through this passive sense. Suppressed signatures still require the normal opposed roll, and Fine Sense or Wide Field information still requires active Chakra Sense.

title: Chakra Suppression
text: The easiest Chakra signature to find is one that does not know it is shouting. You have learned to close the coils down, bury the pressure, and move through the world without advertising what you are.

title: Core Talent
text: You gain Still the Coils: Speed 10, Utility, Self, Concentration Still the Coils — Suppress your Chakra signature until you end this effect or perform an Action that spends Chakra. While suppressed, Chakra sensing does not automatically detect you. When a sensor attempts to locate or identify your signature, oppose their sensing roll with Espionage and gain +10 to your result. Still the Coils conceals your Chakra presence; it does not make your body invisible, silence you, erase footprints, or p

title: Developments
text: Quiet Circulation — Still the Coils becomes Speed 5. The bonus on opposed rolls to conceal your signature becomes +15. Muffled Technique — A Utility or Defensive Action that spends Chakra does not end Still the Coils. An Attack that spends Chakra always ends it unless another rule explicitly says otherwise. False Reading — When you activate Still the Coils, you may choose to leave behind a deliberately misleading surface signature. A sensor who detects you but does not beat your opposed Espionag

title: Mastery
text: Zero Presence — While Still the Coils is active, your bonus on opposed rolls to hide your Chakra becomes +15. Once per battle, when an Action that spends Chakra would end Still the Coils, you may keep the suppression until that Action fully resolves. Observers can still perceive the Action by ordinary means; this only delays the reappearance of your Chakra signature.

title: Rank Benefits
text: Rank benefits are the privileges, instincts and responsibilities a Hunter earns as Haven Ember begins trusting them with more than their own life. Rank is not simply a measure of strength. It is a measure of trust. A stronger Hunter may kill larger things, but a higher-ranked Hunter is somebody Ember trusts with its children, its supplies, its knowledge, and eventually its survival. Strays gain no Rank Benefits. When you reach Trailhand, Huntsman, Warden or Legend, you gain that rank's Automatic

title: Stray
text: Strays are still in training. However talented they may be, Haven Ember has not yet placed enough responsibility on their shoulders for Rank Benefits to represent them. Survive, learn, and earn the right to be trusted.

title: Trailhand
text: You've stopped being somebody else's responsibility. Ember trusts you to leave the walls, do the job, and come back without somebody holding your hand.

title: Take Point — Automatic
text: When you are the designated leader of a group, you may give a specific order to another Hunter up to 3 + XP/1000 times per in-character week. They gain +3 to one relevant roll made directly to carry out that order. If applicable, an ordered attack instead gains +3 Accuracy. Orders must be specific. "Get them out of there," "Hold that door," or "Pin its left leg" qualify. "Do your best" does not. If commanding an ally to take an attack, it must be specific to a subtype. You cannot just say “attac

title: Something to Come Home To
text: Choose a promise, principle, person, or purpose that keeps you moving when you should have stopped. The GMs must approve your choice. Once every 7 OOC days, while directly acting in accordance with it, you may reset your Chakra Exhaustion and Stamina penalties to 0 and reduce your Fatigue by 1. If you knowingly betray that principle, you cannot use this Benefit for 14 OOC days.

title: Too Stubborn to Quit
text: Most people learn when they have reached their limit. You learned to ignore it. You may spend multiple points of Willpower, activations of Limit Break, or similar effects on the same roll, limited only by what you have available.

title: Bring Them Home
text: You've watched enough people leave through Ember's gates without coming back. Whenever an ally is Severely Wounded, Critically Wounded, or reduced to 0 HP, you may trigger this Benefit. Until after your next non-Interrupt Action, you ignore penalties from Fatigue and non-damaging Status Effects. Any Genjutsu currently affecting you is purged, and you gain +5 to defensive Genjutsu rolls during this time. Multiple triggers overlap, but do not stack.

title: Wasteland Conditioning
text: Your body has learned that discomfort is not an emergency. Whenever you Rest, reduce your Stamina penalty by 1 additional point and reduce Suffocation by 1. You may also spend Willpower to reroll a Fatigue Check. Doing so causes you to succeed, making the result of your dice the exact number you needed to pass, even if that number is above 20.

title: Trailwise
text: You've stopped looking at the Wastes and started actually reading them. Once per Hunt, when you fail a Track, Research, Study Weakness or Prepare roll, you may reroll it. You must keep the new result.

title: Hard Country
text: Sometimes there isn't time to stop because you're tired, blinded, freezing, tangled up or halfway dead. As a Speed 0 Action, you may activate or deactivate this Benefit. While active, halve the numerical penalties caused by Fatigue and non-damaging Status Effects. You may maintain this for a total of 50 IC per battle. These ICs do not need to be consecutive.

title: Huntsman
text: You've been outside long enough that people have started asking you what the plan is. Huntsmen lead expeditions, control Ember's outer territories and teach Strays which mistakes only get made once.

title: Pass It Down — Automatic
text: A Haven that does not teach its children dies with its veterans. You may formally train other Hunters in Jutsu you know, allowing them to learn techniques one rank beyond their normal imitation limit. Training takes one week per rank of the technique. You may also teach eligible Capability Talents you possess. This requires one month of training; the student gains the Talent immediately, but their next Talent must be spent paying for it. A character may only owe one Talent at a time.

title: Second Nature
text: You've performed handseals so many thousands of times that your hands barely need to move anymore. If your DEX and always-active Uniques alone could reduce the Seal Speed of a Ninjutsu you know to 0, you may perform it without handseals. This does not apply to Genjutsu, Medical Ninjutsu or Sealing Ninjutsu.

title: Long Haul
text: Strays sprint. Huntsmen know there might still be another twenty miles afterwards. Your bonus to Chakra Exhaustion and Stamina rolls from Fatigue increases by +2 per Fatigue category.

title: Call the Hunt
text: As a Speed 10 Action that cannot be reduced by AP, you may call out up to two Orders. Allies may choose whether to obey. These benefits last 50 IC, or until yo umake anothe order this way. Fallback: +3 to Defensive actions while withdrawing; no hostile Actions while doing so. Gain the ability to attack “retreat” with an attack move. Mark It: +2 Accuracy on the next attack against a target within 3 yards of you. Regroup: +25% Movement while moving toward you or a point within 3 yards of you. Hold

title: Know What You're Killing
text: Once you've seen how something moves, bleeds and reacts, it becomes considerably less mysterious. After your Hunting Team successfully completes Study Weakness against a creature, you gain +2 Accuracy against that creature for the resulting Hunt. Your damage against it is also treated as +25% higher for determining Wounds.

title: Take the Hit
text: Experience has taught you the difference between an attack that hurts and an attack that kills. Once per fight, after seeing the damage of an attack against you, you may spend 1 Willpower to halve the final damage taken.

title: Pack Hunter
text: You don't fight beside people by accident anymore. When an ally successfully damages an enemy, your next attack against that same enemy gains +2 Accuracy. This cannot trigger from your own attacks and does not stack with itself.

title: Warden
text: A Huntsman keeps people alive in the Wastes. A Warden keeps the Haven alive. Researchers. Surgeons. Quartermasters. Engineers. Seal experts. Historians. Scouts. The people who know things nobody else can afford to forget.

title: A Useful Trade — Automatic
text: Choose one Skill appropriate to your work as a Warden. You gain Specialization in that Skill if you did not already possess it. When you roll below a 10 when using that Skill, your d20 roll is instead considered to be a 10, and your maximum ranks in that Skill increase by 3.

title: Practiced Hands
text: There is an enormous difference between knowing something and doing it every day for twenty years. Whenever you spend Willpower to reroll a Skill Roll, add +5 to the final result. You also possess 1 temporary Willpower which can only be used to reroll Skill Rolls and recovers normally.

title: Quartermaster
text: You know where everything goes, who actually needs it, and how much of it mysteriously disappears when nobody keeps count. Whenever you purchase ordinary consumable equipment or field supplies, you receive twice the normal quantity for the same price. This does not apply to Exploding Tags, permanent equipment, weapons, armor or unique items.

title: Expedition Planner
text: You do not leave the gates and hope things work out. Once per Hunt, when a member of your Hunting Team fails a Track, Research, Study Weakness or Prepare roll, you may order a reroll with +3. The new result must be kept.

title: Field Notes
text: Other people see teeth, tracks and corpses. You see information. Once per Hunt, when you personally succeed on Research or Study Weakness, generate 1 additional Intel of the same type.

title: Keep Them Working
text: A Hunt does not stop because somebody is hurt. As a Speed 5 Action, you may end one instance of Stun or Paralysis affecting an ally you can reach and assist.

title: Contingency
text: Wardens have a deeply irritating habit of already having planned for this. Once per battle, after you fail a non-Attack Skill Roll, Fatigue Check, or defensive roll against an environmental hazard, you may declare a contingency and reroll it with +5. You must keep the second result.

title: Legend
text: There is no exam for becoming a Legend. One day you simply realise the children playing Hunter in the streets are pretending to be you. Your name has outgrown you.

title: A Name That Carries — Automatic
text: Within Haven Ember and settlements familiar with its Hunters, your identity is common knowledge. When your reputation would reasonably help you, gain +5 to social Skill Rolls involving authority, trust or intimidation. People may not like you. They have still heard the stories.

title: First to Move
text: People swear they've never seen you surprised. Regardless of your Initiative roll, your first Action in combat always occurs on IC 0.

title: One Clean Hit
text: You've killed enough things to know that battles are often decided by a few inches. Once per battle, when Partial Defense would apply against your attack, you may spend 1 Willpower to ignore all effects of Partial Defense for that attack. Declare this before rolling damage. If the target subsequently avoids the attack entirely, the Willpower is not spent.

title: Marked Quarry
text: Choose one person or creature as your Quarry after spending significant time studying them. You gain +6 Survival to track them, +5 Awareness and Espionage against them, +3 Accuracy against them, and +25% Damage for determining Wounds against them. While fighting your Quarry, you gain 1 temporary Willpower, and another every 50 IC. You may only have one Quarry at a time. It takes a Downtime slot to change quarry.

title: Perfect Ambush
text: Some Legends fought armies. Some simply made sure their enemies never got the opportunity. When attacking someone completely unaware of your presence, your attack gains +4 Accuracy and +25% Damage. You also prepare Sneak Attacks in half the normal required time. This cannot be used simply by hiding from somebody who already knows they are fighting you.

title: Still Standing
text: You've survived at least one thing that should have become the final story anyone ever told about you. Once per fight, after taking damage, you may spend 1 Willpower to halve the final damage taken. If this would still reduce you to 0 HP, you may instead remain at 1 HP. Using the second effect exhausts this Benefit for the remainder of the fight.

title: Against the Impossible
text: There comes a point where monsters stop being warnings and start becoming invitations. When entering battle against a Dread-class or greater Beast, gain 1 temporary Willpower. Every 50 IC you remain actively engaged with that creature, regain that temporary Willpower if it has been spent.

title: Living Myth
text: People fight differently when you're standing beside them. When you spend a point of Willpower, choose one ally who can see or hear you. That ally gains 1 temporary Willpower which lasts until the end of the battle. A character can only benefit from your Living Myth once per battle.

title: Class Benefits
text: Rank tells people how far you've come. Class tells them what they trust you to do when things go wrong. Most Hunters settle naturally into a role over time, shaped by their talents, temperament and the kinds of jobs they keep surviving. To officially join a hunter class, you must complete a number of tasks, by filling in a class sheet, that can be found HERE once you qualify, and officially join the ranks of your chosen class, you gain it’s benefits as listed below.

title: Pathfinder
text: Scouts, trackers and navigators. Pathfinders read broken branches, chakra residue, weather and old roads like other people read books. If something needs finding, following, or reaching alive, you send a Pathfinder.

title: Always a Way
text: You have learned that getting lost is usually just another way of saying you haven't looked hard enough yet. You gain +3 Survival and Awareness when tracking, navigating, locating something, or identifying environmental hazards. Additionally, once per Hunt or Mission, after you or an ally fails a roll involving navigation, tracking, searching, terrain or environmental danger, you may declare that you noticed something they missed. Reroll the check with +5. If successful, you may also ask the GM

title: Slayer
text: The monster killers. Slayers specialise in putting dangerous things into the ground quickly and permanently. Heavy hitters, duelists and shinobi whose first answer to a problem is usually violence.

title: Bring it Down
text: You have stopped thinking about monsters as enormous creatures. They're collections of things that can break. Whenever you deal enough damage to potentially cause a Wound, treat your damage as +25% higher for determining whether a Wound occurs.

title: Anchor
text: Protectors and defenders. Anchors hold lines, guard caravans, protect settlements and make sure the rest of the team gets home. When everyone else runs, an Anchor is usually the one standing in the way.

title: Nobody Gets Through
text: When you're standing between danger and somebody else, moving you becomes the difficult part. Whenever an enemy attacks an ally within 3 yards of you, you may spend 1 Willpower to Intercept without paying the normal additional cost or penalty associated with doing so, causing the attack to be targeting you, and nobody else.. Additionally, when you successfully defend against an attack or Intercept one for another character, you may Hold the Line until after your next Action. While holding the li

title: Trapper
text: Hunters who win before the fight begins. Seals, snares, explosives, poisons, ambushes and prepared terrain. A good Trapper turns an impossible Hunt into a fair one. You don't fight fair. You fight prepared. Whenever you successfully complete Prepare during a Hunt, you create one additional Preparation. Additionally, once per battle you may reveal a reasonable piece of equipment, environmental preparation, seal, trap, marked position or precaution that you could have established beforehand. Decla

title: Scavenger
text: Salvagers, harvesters and survivalists. Scavengers know what is worth carrying home, how to strip a beast clean, and how to turn ruins into food, tools, medicine and money. Other Hunters see wreckage.You see tomorrow's supplies.
